title: Why Google Still Matters: The Real Data Behind AI Search Hype
summary: AI is projected to match Google’s conversion performance by late 2027 to early 2028. Businesses adopting it now will gain a giant edge over competitors.
body_text: In a Nutshell Google is still the dominant platform for organic conversions, though AI search converts at 4 to 5 times the rate, paving the way for a coming tipping point Our informal estimate is AI could drive equal conversions to Google by late 2027 to early 2028 Companies starting AI visibility now have roughly 18-24 months to lay the groundwork before AI potentially drives the same number of leads as Google Table of Contents Why Google Still Drives 90% of Your Conversions Why AI Traffic Converts Better Despite Lower Numbers When AI Could Match Google for Conversions: Our Informal Analysis AI Search Grew 527% Year-Over-Year: What This Means for Your Marketing Budget The Integrated Approach: Why "Both" Is Your Only Real Option What Startups Should Do Right Now Why Google Still Drives 90% of Your Conversions You have limited budget. AI search gets all the headlines. Does Google still matter? Let's look at the actual numbers. Every startup founder faces this question right now. The media narrative screams that traditional SEO is dead. ChatGPT, Perplexity and Claude dominate tech Twitter. Your competitors are pivoting their entire content strategy to AI optimization. The pressure to abandon Google and bet everything on AI search feels overwhelming. Here's what the data actually shows: Google still dominates by massive margins. Google processes 16.4 billion searches daily. ChatGPT handles 2.5 billion prompts, but only about a third of those are searches for information (not creative tasks or conversations). That brings the real comparison to roughly 800 million AI searches versus Google's 16.4 billion. Research Finding: ChatGPT reached 2.5 billion daily prompts by July 2025 , with approximately one-third representing searches for information rather than creative tasks or conversations. The volume difference is staggering, but it's only part of the story. Google maintains approximately 90% market share (ranging between 89-93% throughout 2025), while AI platforms currently drive less than 1% of global web traffic. Research Finding: AI platforms account for less than 1% of global internet traffic as of early 2025, compared to 48.5% from organic search , (with the balance from direct, social, referral, and other sources), according to SE Ranking's analysis of 63,987 websites with Google Analytics data showing figures as low as 0.15% across most industries. For SaaS companies specifically, these numbers may be higher, potentially accelerating the shift toward AI conversions. For most startups, Google drives 90% or more of search-driven conversions today. The volume gap isn't close. But before you dismiss AI search entirely, here's what those raw numbers don't tell you about conversion quality. Why AI Traffic Converts Better Despite Lower Numbers Raw volume isn't the full story. AI search traffic shows something remarkable: superior engagement and conversion rates that change the entire competitive equation. The AI Engagement Advantage: Why Longer Sessions Drive More Conversions AI traffic doesn't just convert better. It converts at rates that fundamentally change the economics of search visibility. Research Finding: Analysis of 12 million website visits shows AI traffic converts at rates 4-5x higher than Google on average, with results ranging from small gains to 9x depending on industry and implementation quality. The average AI visitor converts at 14.2% compared to Google's 2.8%, with platform leaders showing conversion rates from Claude at 16.8%, ChatGPT at 14.2%, and Perplexity at 12.4%. Why the conversion advantage? AI users arrive with different intent. They've already researched, compared alternatives and refined their requirements through conversation with an AI assistant. When they click through to your site, they're further along the buyer journey. They convert faster. Research Finding: Pew Research's October 2025 study reveals users click 47% less with AI Overviews in Google results (8% click rate with AI Overviews vs 15% without). More telling: 26% end their browsing session entirely after getting AI-generated answers, compared to just 16% without AI Overviews. This isn't about AI stealing Google's traffic. It's about a fundamental shift in how people search and make decisions. They got what they needed without clicking. How AI Drives Equal Conversions with Only a Quarter of the Traffic The conversion advantage creates a counterintuitive reality: AI doesn't need to match Google's volume to match its results. With a 4-5x conversion advantage, AI only needs roughly 25% of total traffic to generate the same number of conversions as Google's 75% of total traffic. Let's make this concrete. Today, if your startup gets 3,000 monthly visitors split 99% Google and 1% AI: Google generates roughly 83 conversions (at a 2.8% conversion rate) AI generates 4 conversions (at a 14.2% conversion rate) Google dominates, AI barely registers But as AI's traffic share grows, that quality advantage compounds. When AI reaches 25% of your traffic with Google at 75% of it, the math shifts dramatically: Google generates 63 conversions AI generates 107 conversions Suddenly AI is your primary conversion driver despite being the minority traffic source The tipping point isn't about volume parity. It's about when quality overtakes quantity for actual business results. Note: Comprehensive analysis of prompt types is only available for ChatGPT (32.7% of prompts are searches for information). We apply this figure conservatively across general-purpose AI assistants, recognizing search-focused platforms like Perplexity likely have higher percentages. Here's when our analysis suggests that crossover could happen. ‍ When AI Could Match Google for Conversions: Our Informal Analysis When will AI search drive more conversions than Google? Based on some back-of-the-envelope calculations using current data, we estimate this tipping point could happen somewhere between late 2027 and early 2028, giving you roughly 18-24 months to position strategically. How We're Thinking About This We ran some informal calculations based on publicly available data: AI currently sits at less than 1% of website traffic with a 4-5x conversion advantage, meaning it needs about 25% market share to match Google's conversion volume. If AI growth moderates to 100-200% annually (significantly slower than recent explosive growth but still strong), that puts the crossover somewhere between late 2027 and early 2028. These are back-of-the-envelope projections, not predictions. Your mileage will vary based on your industry and how well you optimize for AI platforms. When AI Becomes Your Primary Conversion Driver Here's how the numbers could play out: Timeline Google Traffic Share AI Traffic Share Google Conv Rate AI Conv Rate Conversion Split Today (Oct 2025) 99% <1% 2.8% 14.2% Google dominates Mid 2026 90% 10% 2.8% 14.2% Google 64% / AI 36% Late 2027 75% 25% 2.8% 14.2% EQUAL ~50/50 Early 2028 35% 2.8% 65% 14.2% AI leads 63% / Google 37% How to read this: Using the conversion rates from earlier (2.8% for Google traffic and 14.2% for AI traffic), AI needs about 25% of total traffic to generate the same number of conversions as Google's 75%. Methodology Note: This analysis assumes Google maintains 2.8% average conversion rates while AI platforms achieve a 14.2% conversion rate (based on Superprompt's 12M visit study). Our AI traffic share projections use conservative 100-200% annual growth rates, though some studies support a much higher annual growth rate. Actual timing depends on sustained growth and platform-specific optimization quality. Individual results vary by industry and implementation. This timeline assumes current trends continue; significant changes in AI platform policies or Google's AI Overviews could shift timing. These are illustrative scenarios based on our informal analysis, not precise forecasts. The actual timeline depends on variables like sustained growth rates and whether AI platforms maintain their conversion advantage. Your 18-24 Month Window to Get Ready for the AI Shift The timeline creates three distinct positioning scenarios: 01 Start Now (Q4 2025) You have 6 months to build your AI visibility foundation through Q2 2026, then 6 months for optimization and refinement through Q4 2026. You're positioned when the tipping point potentially arrives in late 2027. You capture the advantage as the shift accelerates. 02 Wait Until 2026 You start in early-to-mid 2026 and spend 6-12 months building visibility. You're positioned by mid-2027, several months before the potential tipping point arrives. The disadvantage: competitors who started now have 12-18 months of accumulated citations, authority signals and platform training that you're starting without. They've been compounding while you've been planning. 03 Wait Until Late 2027 By the time you recognize AI drives equal conversions, competition has a 12-18 month head start. You spend 2028-2029 closing the gap while they compound their advantage. Key Insight: Late 2027 isn't a deadline. It's when AI conversions could equal Google's based on current trends. Companies positioning now will be ready when the shift arrives. Companies positioning later will be playing catchup. These estimates are based on real growth data. Here's what the numbers show. AI Search Grew 527% Year-Over-Year: What This Means for Your Marketing Budget The timeline projection isn't speculation. It's extrapolation from documented year-over-year growth rates that validate the urgency. Why 527% Growth Validates Our 2027-2028 Estimate Research Finding: A 19-site study found AI platform traffic grew 527% year-over-year comparing January-May 2025 to the same period in 2024, signaling rapid mainstream adoption of AI search platforms. This explosive pace will likely moderate as the market matures. Even with significant deceleration, the crossover could arrive within the next 2-3 years. What does sustained strong growth mean for companies building visibility now? Early positioning creates compound advantages. Every month you're visible in AI platforms builds authority, accumulates citations and trains the models to reference you. Companies starting today have 18-24 months of compounding before AI becomes the primary conversion driver. Why waiting means facing more competition for limited AI visibility: AI platforms don't show 10 blue links. They cite 2-3 authoritative sources. The earlier you establish authority, the harder it becomes for competitors to displace you. User behavior is shifting rapidly as AI-first search experiences become mainstream. So if you can't ignore either channel, what does an integrated strategy actually look like? The Integrated Approach: Why "Both" Is Your Only Real Option The data reveals a clear strategic imperative: you need both channels, optimized for their distinct strengths, working together. The Foundation Layer: Traditional SEO That Funds Operations Google captures existing demand at scale and drives revenue today. This isn't about nostalgia for "the way things used to be." It's about business fundamentals. Google's massive daily search volume represents real people with real intent looking for solutions right now. That volume funds your operations, extends your runway and generates the cash flow that lets you invest in future positioning. Traditional SEO creates the content foundation that AI platforms can cite. Every ranking article, every authoritative resource and every detailed guide you build for Google becomes source material for AI responses. The technical infrastructure serves both channels: schema markup, structured data and clear content organization help both Google's crawlers and AI's training data understand what you offer. The data you generate from traditional SEO optimizes your entire approach. You learn which topics resonate, which phrases convert and which content formats drive results. That intelligence informs your AI strategy. The Future Layer: AI Visibility That Captures Intent AI visibility positions your content for AI platform citations. When ChatGPT, Perplexity or Claude answer questions in your category, your company should be the authoritative source they reference. This captures emerging high-intent traffic before competition intensifies. Key Insight: The conversion advantage varies significantly by implementation quality. This makes strategic positioning now even more critical than the timeline itself. Companies optimizing for AI platforms today will see superior conversion rates. Companies waiting will face more competition for fewer opportunities to be cited as a source. AI visibility sets up compound growth effects. Each citation builds authority. Each authority signal increases future citation probability. The flywheel accelerates for early movers. The Integration Points The most effective strategy doesn't choose between channels. It creates content that ranks on Google AND gets cited by AI platforms simultaneously. The measurement frameworks track both channels to understand your complete search visibility picture. RankScience's integrated methodology optimizes content for both Google rankings and AI platform citations. Rather than choosing between traditional SEO and AI optimization, we help startups capture both channels strategically with limited resources. Here's what this means for your startup's growth strategy. What Startups Should Do Right Now The strategic choice isn't Google or AI. It's how you capture both the volume that funds your business today and the quality that could become your primary conversion driver by late 2027. Don't abandon traditional SEO. Google's massive daily search volume still drives 90% of conversions today. The reports of SEO's death are greatly exaggerated. For the next 18-24 months minimum, Google remains your primary traffic source and revenue driver. Don't ignore AI visibility. Our calculations suggest the tipping point could arrive between late 2027 and early 2028, giving you roughly 18-24 months to position strategically. The companies that establish authority in AI platforms before the crossover will have compound advantages that are difficult for competitors to overcome. Implement both strategically. Your content foundation should serve both channels from day one. This isn't about doubling your workload. It's about optimizing the content you're already creating for both Google's algorithms and AI's training data. Your Four-Step Action Plan 01 Audit your current visibility Where do you appear in Google versus ChatGPT, Perplexity, Gemini, Google AI Overviews and Claude? Most startups have strong Google visibility but zero AI presence. That gap represents risk. A quick AI visibility audit will show you where you stand and what you can improve. 02 Optimize for both channels Implement technical optimizations and content patterns that AI platforms prefer while maintaining Google SEO best practices. This requires specialized knowledge of how each platform evaluates and cites content. The technical overlap is significant. Much of what helps AI also helps Google. 03 Measure both channels Track traditional organic traffic AND AI platform referrals to understand your complete search visibility picture. You can't optimize what you don't measure. Set up tracking now while AI traffic is still small. You'll see the growth in real time. 04 Start positioning now AI visibility typically takes 3-6 months to establish meaningful traction, with momentum continuing to build beyond that through 12+ months. Authority accumulates through consistent optimization, quality content and technical excellence. The earlier you start, the better positioned you'll be when the potential tipping point arrives. The bottom line: The question isn't "Google or AI?" The question is "How do I capture both the Google volume that funds my business today and the AI conversion quality that could become my primary conversion driver by late 2027?" Companies that answer this question strategically will be positioned before the potential tipping point rather than scrambling to catch up. title: TransUnion Brings New Alternative Credit Signals to Mortgage Decisioning
summary: TransUnion (NYSE: TRU) today announced an enhancement to its mortgage credit report, with the addition of TruVision™ Alternative Credit Attributes (ACA 2.0) from its FactorTrust® Alternative Lending Database to expand lenders’ visibility beyond traditional credit data.The new alternative credit attributes give lenders earlier insight into b...
body_text: Chicago, 16 July 2026 | 07:17 AM America/Chicago TransUnion Brings New Alternative Credit Signals to Mortgage Decisioning Alternative Credit Attributes advance TransUnion’s legacy of innovation with more comprehensive data for smarter mortgage decisions TransUnion (NYSE: TRU) today announced an enhancement to its mortgage credit report, with the addition of TruVision™ Alternative Credit Attributes (ACA 2.0) from its FactorTrust® Alternative Lending Database to expand lenders’ visibility beyond traditional credit data. The new alternative credit attributes give lenders earlier insight into borrower stability and intent, enabling them to prioritize high-potential applicants earlier in the funnel, streamline workflows and focus resources on loans more likely to convert. Applied as early as the prequalification stage, the data helps reduce risk sooner in the decisioning process. It also supports more consistent underwriting and enables competitive pricing for qualified borrowers. By layering alternative financial signals alongside traditional credit data, the new ACA 2.0 attributes deepen mortgage risk assessments and provide greater visibility into the consumer’s full wallet. Moreover, these enhanced insights are delivered at no additional cost, enabling lenders to improve decision quality without increasing underwriting expense. “ This enhancement reflects our continued focus on giving mortgage lenders a more complete and actionable view of borrower behavior. By bringing richer credit insight earlier into the process, lenders can make more confident decisions, reduce unnecessary risk and concentrate their efforts on applicants most likely to convert—ultimately enabling more efficient access to credit for qualified consumers. Satyan Merchant, senior vice president, auto and mortgage business leader at TransUnion „ Continuing a History of Mortgage Lending Innovation This latest enhancement to the mortgage credit report builds on TransUnion’s legacy of innovation that helps lenders better assess consumer creditworthiness. These include: · Trended Credit Data: In 2013, TransUnion introduced first-to-market trended credit data, shifting underwriting away from a single point-in-time snapshot toward a more dynamic view of borrower behavior. This helps reshape risk assessment, segmentation and approaches to fairer pricing. · TruVision Early Access Soft Check : This solution delivers comprehensive credit insights without a hard inquiry, enabling smarter prequalification decisions. It brings rich TransUnion data earlier into the mortgage process, improving operational efficiency and transparency for both lenders and borrowers. “TransUnion continues to expand credit insight through our risk solutions,” said Mohamed Abdelsadek, Chief Global Solutions Officer, TransUnion. “Combined with TruVision™ Alternative Credit Attributes, these innovations give lenders greater confidence and a more complete, dynamic view of consumer financial behavior.” To learn more about TransUnion Mortgage Industry Solutions that help lenders make smarter, more confident marketing, customer acquisition and lending decisions, click here . Boilerplate About TransUnion (NYSE: TRU) TransUnion is a global information and insights company with over 13,000 associates operating in more than 30 countries. We make trust possible by ensuring each person is reliably represented in the marketplace. We do this with a Tru™ picture of each person: an actionable view of consumers, stewarded with care. Through our acquisitions and technology investments we have developed innovative solutions that extend beyond our strong foundation in core credit into areas such as marketing, fraud, risk and advanced analytics. As a result, consumers and businesses can transact with confidence and achieve great things. We call this Information for Good® — and it leads to economic opportunity, great experiences and personal empowerment for millions of people around the world. http://www.transunion.com/business

title: 7 Best Email Clients for Accounting Firms in 2026 (Free and Paid)
body_text: Key Takeaways Accounting firms that add Finlens to their email stack reduce client email volume by up to 80% during month-end close, eliminating document-chasing threads before they start In 2024, the IRS recorded 250+ data breach reports from tax professionals, impacting more than 200,000 clients making email security non-negotiable for any firm Microsoft Outlook 365 remains the most compliant email platform for firms governed by the IRS Safeguards Rule and the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act (GLBA) Karbon, at $59–$99/user/month, is the best single platform combining email sync, workflow, and client management for mid-to-large accounting firms Missive starts at $14/user/month and is the strongest shared inbox option for teams of 5–50 who cannot justify Karbon's pricing Why Choosing an Email Client for Accounting Firms Is Different Most articles on email clients compare speed, design, and plugin ecosystems. That advice is built for sales teams and startups. Accounting firms have a different problem. Your inbox is a compliance surface, a document exchange channel, and a client communication record all at once. The misconception most firm owners arrive with: "I just need a better inbox." The real problem: for accounting firms, the inbox reflects a broken workflow. Every email you send to chase a payroll file, every thread asking for a bank statement, every reply telling a client their close is delayed these are workflow failures that show up as email volume. Three specific failure modes hit accounting firms hardest: Security gap. Regular email clients send sensitive financial data unencrypted. The FTC's updated Safeguards Rule requires firms to encrypt client data in transit and at rest. Most standard inboxes do not meet this standard without additional configuration. Inbox fragmentation. When five staff members share a single client@firm.com address in their individual Gmail accounts, emails get missed, duplicate replies get sent, and no one owns the thread. Workflow-email disconnect. Standard email clients have no knowledge of deadlines, client status, or outstanding tasks. Security and Compliance Coverage Your email platform is a compliance surface. Team Collaboration Features Solo practitioners need speed. Firms with 3+ staff need assignment, shared read status, and internal commenting. Integration with Your Accounting Software If your platform cannot see your QBO or Xero data, you will spend time manually cross-referencing client information across tabs. Karbon integrates with Outlook, Gmail, and Exchange. Canopy integrates natively with QBO, Xero, and Intuit ProConnect. Finlens connects directly with QBO for close data. Verify which integrations your chosen platform includes at the plan you are actually buying, not the enterprise tier. 4. Email Volume Per Client A firm with 10 clients sending 5 emails per client per month generates 50 client emails monthly. A firm with 50 clients generates 250. Platforms like Missive and Karbon handle high volume through assignment queues. Standard inboxes do not scale beyond 30–40 active client relationships without becoming unmanageable. Finlens' close automation reduces client email generation at the source, which changes the volume equation entirely. 5. Total Cost at Your Team Size Most email platforms charge per user. Gmail is sufficient for a solo practitioner managing fewer than 10 clients with no team members. For firms with multiple staff sharing client communication, Gmail without a shared inbox layer creates missed emails, duplicate replies, and no audit trail. Most firms with 3+ staff benefit from Missive, Karbon, or Cone on top of their Gmail or Outlook account. Is there a free email client for accounting firms? Yes. Finlens offers a free plan (no credit card required) that automates close-related client communication and reduces the email volume your inbox needs to handle. For a traditional shared inbox, Missive's trial is available, but the paid tier starts at $14/user/month. Most practice management platforms with email do not have free tiers. How is Finlens different from other email clients for accounting firms? Finlens is not an email client in the traditional sense. It is the automation layer that prevents most accounting emails from being generated in the first place. Instead of chasing clients manually via email for documents, follow-ups, and status updates, Finlens sends automated sequences on your behalf and shows clients real-time close status. This means firms using Finlens can manage their remaining email with any standard client, since volume drops dramatically. Is Microsoft Outlook compliant with IRS data protection requirements? Yes, but only with the right plan. Microsoft 365 Business Premium ($22/user/month) includes Microsoft Defender for Office 365, Safe Links, Safe Attachments, and anti-impersonation protection features the IRS Security Summit recommends for tax professionals. The entry-level Microsoft 365 Business Basic ($6/user/month) does not include these protections. Firms handling sensitive client financial data should budget for Business Premium or Business Standard with Defender add-ons. Can Karbon replace my email client entirely? Karbon integrates with your existing Gmail, Outlook, or Microsoft Exchange account rather than replacing it. Emails flow into Karbon's Triage inbox where they become actionable work items, but they also remain in your Gmail or Outlook inbox. Most Karbon users keep their original email account and manage client-facing correspondence inside Karbon while using their personal inbox for internal admin. What email platform do most accounting firms use? Microsoft Outlook is the most common email platform among accounting firms, particularly firms in the US with 5+ staff. A 2024 survey by Karbon found that more than 60% of accounting practices still run on Microsoft 365. Smaller firms and solo practitioners are more likely to use Gmail and Google Workspace, primarily for cost and interface simplicity. Do I need to migrate my existing email to use Karbon or Missive? No. Both Karbon and Missive connect to your existing Gmail, Outlook, or Exchange account. You keep your existing email address and inbox. The platform adds a collaboration layer on top. There is no data migration required. How does email security for accounting firms differ from standard business email security? Accounting firms handle nonpublic personal information (NPPI) Social Security numbers, bank account details, tax records that is explicitly covered by the GLBA Safeguards Rule. This means accounting firms face stricter requirements than most small businesses: written risk assessments, encryption in transit and at rest, MFA for any system accessing client data, and a designated information security officer. Standard email for a retail business does not carry these obligations. Accounting firms that treat email as a general business tool without compliance configuration risk FTC fines of up to $100,000 per violation. ‍ ‍

title: Understand the impact of your crude oil supply chain
summary: Upstream emissions play a crucial role in determining the carbon intensity of crude oil. Discover why accurate accounting is key for compliance and financial stability.
body_text: Understand the impact of your crude oil supply chain In spite of the fact that oil demand is on course to plateau by 2030, it remains the most widely used energy source globally, despite growing pressure to decarbonise. As economies transition toward net zero, the oil industry faces a fundamental challenge: unlike metals and minerals, there is no credible decarbonisation pathway for crude oil . The only way to significantly reduce its emissions is to use less of it — a reality that companies with oil exposure must prepare for. What about carbon capture, utilization, and storage (CCUS)? The oil industry often places a strong emphasis on CCUS as a way to decarbonise fossil energy, however: investment and capacity, even in the most optimistic cases, is not enough to be a credible pathway to meet net zero targets in 2050. With that said, upstream emissions do account for 10–30% of crude oil’s footprint. In this article, we break down how emissions vary across the crude oil supply chain, why understanding your oil intensity is critical, and how asset-level carbon data can help companies comply with regulations, manage financial risk, and make informed low-carbon decisions. What is crude oil’s carbon footprint? Oil demand growth is expected to slow through this decade. But today, oil demand persists, accounting for 33% of global CO2 emissions from fossil fuel combustion. The petrochemical sector continues to drive consumption, and industries from transportation to heavy manufacturing remain reliant on oil-derived products. Meanwhile, regulatory frameworks such as the EU’s Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM) are set to impose stricter carbon pricing on carbon-intensive imports (for which crude oil refined is often used as a fuel source in manufacturing), increasing financial and compliance risks for businesses that fail to track their emissions. While emissions vary significantly across different industrial materials, most of oil’s carbon impact occurs at the point of combustion — when it’s mostly used as fuel. Unlike metals, where emissions vary based on ore quality, energy sources, processing and recycling methods, the vast majority of crude oil’s emissions are locked in from the moment it’s extracted. Yet, upstream emissions from extraction, refining, and transport still play a crucial role in determining the total carbon intensity of a barrel of oil. For businesses that buy, trade, or finance crude oil, these supply chain emissions matter. In Europe, for example, the carbon intensity of imported crude oils ranges from 4–50 grams of CO2 equivalent per megajoule (g CO2e/MJ) with an average of 12 g CO2 e/MJ. As we’ll see in the coming sections, relying on industry averages is not something we recommend — though it can be useful to know how averages vary across regions. In the next section, we break down the four key stages of crude oil emissions and how they impact total carbon intensity. What causes crude oil’s emissions? While the majority of crude oil’s emissions occur when its refined products are burned as fuel, significant emissions are generated before it ever reaches the end user. Understanding where emissions originate in the crude oil supply chain is critical for businesses looking to measure, manage, and report their carbon footprint accurately. What drives crude oil’s life cycle emissions? The carbon footprint of crude oil varies depending on several factors. Let’s break it down by stage: 1. Extraction and processing Production techniques — some oil reserves are more difficult to explore and require energy intensive oil recovery techniques such as water and gas reinjection, fracking, steam flooding or upgrading. Some oil production sites have fully switched to renewable electricity. Gas flaring — the amount of gas flared is a significant differentiator for carbon intensity of crude oil. Special attention is paid to so-called routine flaring that refers to the continuous combustion of associated gas during standard oil production operations when there are insufficient facilities or suitable geological conditions to re-inject the gas, utilize it on-site, or transport it to a market. Methane emissions — methane is 80 times more potent than CO₂ over a 20-year period, making its emissions a major contributor to crude oil’s footprint. Typical sources of methane emissions include unburnt methane from gas flaring, gas venting during maintenance activities, process vents, small leaks, and seeps from the equipment and uncontrolled material releases. 2. Transport & distribution Distance and transportation mode affect the total footprint. Crude oil needs to be delivered first to the export hub or storage terminal, consumed locally or transported to global locations to be refined (e.g. via crude oil tankers). Then, refined products need to be distributed to end users. For example, transportation on a conventional truck would be much more carbon intensive than transportation via pipelines or vessels. The recent shift toward non-Russian oil and tensions, including those involving the Red Sea shipping corridor, have led to increased transportation costs and emissions, and increased demand for long-haul shipping as oil routes shift from Russia-to-Europe to Russia-to-Asia. 3. Refining ‍ Refining crude into usable fuels is highly energy-intensive and can account for 3–10% of a barrel’s total emissions. The energy intensity of refining depends on the crude’s quality and the complexity of the refinery configuration. Some refineries are far more carbon-intensive than others due to: Energy source (carbon intensity of supplied electricity, on-site generation). Refining complexity (heavy crude requires more processing). 4. End-use emissions Emissions for crude oil vary depending on the end use case , too. Combustion is the base case for fuels, however some refined products are not made to be combusted, like lube oils. Products of the petrochemical industry can also have different end of life treatment, that can include recycling and landfill. 70–90% of oil’s lifecycle emissions come from burning oil-derived fuels , with indirect emissions accounting for only 10–30% of oil’s lifecycle emissions intensity. Below is an example of how significant each source of emissions could be, based on IEA’s Spectrum of the well-to-tank emissions intensity of global oil production, 2018: Because of these variables, the embodied carbon in purchased crude oil can vary significantly. Businesses that rely on industry-wide averages may be under- or overestimating their true emissions. According to the IEA, the most-emitting sources of oil produce more than four times the indirect emissions than the least-emitting sources. This is why when it comes to carbon accounting, it’s so important to understand your specific commodity and its corresponding supply chain. So what’s the takeaway? Businesses exposed to crude oil supply chains must track emissions at every stage, not just at the point of combustion. The choice of crude source, extraction method, refining pathway, and transport mode all influence the total carbon footprint, making granular supply chain data critical for accurate reporting. Why crude oil emissions vary by region The carbon intensity of crude oil varies significantly by region, driven by differences in extraction methods, resource quality, energy inputs, and transport distances. The visualization below, based on data from the article by Masnadi et al. (2018) , shows how the carbon intensity of crude oil production can vary depending on the country of origin: ‍ Here’s a glimpse at some regional differences in crude oil emissions: Middle Eastern crude: ‍ Thanks to large, productive reservoirs, Middle Eastern crude typically has lower emissions associated with each barrel due to ease of extraction. The above-mentioned study shows a low carbon intensity of 4.6 grams of CO2e per megajoule, or approximately 27 kg of CO2 e per barrel. Many fields have low levels of flaring and venting, which means less methane emissions. Some regions in this area boast a flaring intensity level of less than 1% . Canadian oil sands: ‍ This region has traditionally been categorized among the highest-emission crude sources due to energy-intensive extraction and upgrading processes. Oil sands must be heated with steam (steam-assisted gravity drainage, SAGD) or mined and processed, both of which require large amounts of fuel and water. Methane flaring and venting further increase emissions. However, progress has been made, with the average greenhouse gas (GHG) intensity of Canadian oil sands having fallen by 23% since 2009. In 2022, mined synthetic crude oil averaged 86 kg CO2e per barrel . US shale oil: ‍ Carbon intensity varies widely depending on well efficiency and methane management. For example: The Permian and Delaware basins have a carbon intensity of about 18.1 kgCO2e per barrel of oil equivalent (boe) The Louisiana Gulf Coast area reaches 95.4 kgCO2e/boe Tight oil (fracked shale) is typically more carbon-intensive due to the large number of wells and energy used for drilling and hydraulic fracturing. Methane leaks from production and gathering systems can significantly increase lifecycle emissions. Recent research indicates that oil and gas operations across the US are emitting more than 6 million tons of methane per year, with total leaked emissions ranging from less than 1% to as much as 9.6% of total volume, averaging 3% across surveyed regions. Deepwater offshore crude: Offshore drilling can have high production emissions due to energy-intensive operations. That said, once operational, deepwater fields can have lower emissions per barrel compared to other sources due to efficient extraction, high productivity, and minimal flaring. For example, deepwater production in the Gulf of Mexico had a production-weighted average GHG intensity of 7 kg CO2e/boe in 2022, which is lower than many other oil-producing regions. Deepwater offshore wells consume more energy and require more material for construction, leading to higher initial GHG emissions. However, these emissions are offset by the higher well productivity of offshore deepwater fields. Offshore producers have an average emissions intensity of approximately 17 kg per boe , with the vast majority of operators falling in the 10-40 kg per boe range. Understanding why and where crude oil emissions intensity varies is important, but what does it mean for companies ? Here’s why tracking your crude oil supply chain matters now more than ever. Why tracking your crude oil supply chain matters Regulations are evolving Carbon pricing mechanisms like the EU CBAM and UK CBAM are putting a carbon price on carbon-intensive commodities, many of which are manufactured through using crude oil as a fuel source. And regulatory frameworks like the EU’s Corporate Sustainability Reporting Directive (CSRD) require more detailed Scope 3 emissions reporting, including fossil fuel-related emissions. The upcoming EU ETS2 , set to start in 2027 as part of the Fit for 55 package, will cover emissions from road transport and buildings. In this system, fuel suppliers will be responsible for the emissions associated with the fuels they place on the market, effectively addressing upstream emissions. Non-compliant companies will face a range of penalties, including subsidy suspension and financial penalties. Investor and lender scrutiny is increasing Financial institutions are shifting away from high-carbon assets; major investors and banks are reducing exposure to unreported or high-carbon supply chains. Additionally, sustainability-linked finance is growing. Many banks now offer preferential lending rates for businesses that demonstrate carbon transparency and reduction efforts. Failure to disclose emissions increases financial risk — without accurate data, businesses may face higher capital costs, difficulty securing financing, or investor divestment. Corporate climate targets demand accurate emissions data For those companies that have committed to net-zero goals, sourcing lower-carbon crude and optimizing refining and transport choices can reduce overall corporate emissions intensity. Tracking oil supply chain emissions can also help to enable smarter procurement decisions that align with climate targets and regulatory expectations. Reputational risks are increasing Transparency on supply chain emissions is key as scrutiny of fossil fuel investments increases. Stakeholder pressure is growing — customers, investors, and regulators are demanding more carbon data. Transparency can be a competitive advantage. Businesses that measure and disclose their crude oil life cycle emissions accurately can differentiate themselves in an increasingly carbon-conscious market. Tracking the emissions intensity of your crude oil supply chain is now a business necessity. Companies that understand their supply chain emissions will be better positioned to comply with evolving regulations, secure financing, and reduce climate-related business risks. How to measure crude oil emissions accurately Many businesses rely on global average emissions factors to estimate their crude oil footprint, but this approach can be highly misleading. The carbon intensity of crude oil varies by extraction method, refinery efficiency, transport mode, and origin. Asset-level data is essential for accurate reporting and regulatory compliance. CarbonChain: ‍The industry standard solution for carbon management CarbonChain’s platform provides supply chain-specific carbon intensity calculations based on real-world assets. With CarbonChain, companies can: → Identify the lowest-carbon crude sources → Understand the emissions impact of their refining and distribution choices → Report oil-related emissions with accuracy for regulatory compliance How CarbonChain helps businesses track and reduce crude oil emissions Crude oil remains a dominant energy source, but its emissions intensity is under increasing scrutiny. Businesses interested in managing their financial, regulatory, and reputational risks — as all businesses should be — must focus on tracking, managing, and reducing their oil-related emissions to remain compliant and competitive. title: Cómo funciona el scoring invisible en fintech y por qué está cambiando el acceso financiero
summary: ¿Cómo las fintech evalúan perfiles financieros? Descubre cómo funciona el scoring invisible en fintech y por qué es importante.
body_text: ¡Ahora puedes solicitar tu crédito por whatsapp! Sin papeleos ni complicaciones Pídelo ahora Durante muchos años, el acceso a productos financieros dependió principalmente del historial crediticio tradicional. Sin embargo, los cambios en la economía y el crecimiento de trabajadores independientes, emprendedores y personas con poca experiencia crediticia han impulsado nuevas formas de evaluar el perfil financiero de los usuarios. Una de ellas es el scoring invisible , un modelo utilizado por las fintech que complementa la evaluación tradicional mediante el análisis de información relacionada con el comportamiento financiero cotidiano. Su objetivo no es reemplazar el historial crediticio ni garantizar la aprobación de un crédito, sino ofrecer una visión más amplia de la realidad económica de cada persona. Gracias al uso de análisis de datos, inteligencia artificial y procesos automatizados, este enfoque permite identificar patrones financieros antes difíciles de detectar, haciendo las evaluaciones más ágiles y contribuyendo a ampliar las oportunidades de inclusión financiera para un mayor número de personas. En este artículo conocerás qué es el scoring invisible, qué tipo de información puede aportar a una evaluación financiera más completa y cómo funcionan las fintech para liderar esta transformación. Qué es el scoring invisible y cómo se diferencia de los modelos tradicionales El scoring invisible es una metodología que utiliza información complementaria para enriquecer la evaluación financiera de una persona. Mientras los modelos tradicionales se concentran principalmente en variables como el historial crediticio, las obligaciones financieras y el comportamiento frente a créditos anteriores, el scoring invisible incorpora señales adicionales relacionadas con la actividad financiera cotidiana. La diferencia principal está en el enfoque. Los modelos tradicionales observan principalmente el pasado financiero registrado en productos de crédito. Los modelos más modernos también analizan cómo una persona administra sus recursos en el presente. Esto permite construir una visión más amplia sobre aspectos como: Organización financiera. Actividad económica. Regularidad de determinados comportamientos. Uso de herramientas financieras digitales. Evolución de ciertos hábitos financieros. El objetivo no consiste en reemplazar la evaluación tradicional, sino en complementarla mediante información que refleje mejor la realidad económica de muchos usuarios. Esto resulta especialmente útil para personas que aún no cuentan con un historial crediticio amplio, pero mantienen hábitos financieros responsables. Qué tipo de información puede ayudar a construir una evaluación financiera alternativa Las nuevas tecnologías permiten analizar diferentes tipos de información que ayudan a comprender mejor el comportamiento financiero. No se trata de observar una compra específica ni una única transferencia. Lo importante es identificar patrones consistentes a lo largo del tiempo. Algunos ejemplos de información que puede contribuir a una evaluación más amplia son: Actividad transaccional La frecuencia con la que una persona realiza movimientos financieros puede aportar información sobre su nivel de actividad económica. Regularidad de ingresos Los ingresos constantes permiten observar estabilidad, incluso cuando provienen de diferentes fuentes. Hábitos de pago La organización para cumplir con compromisos financieros refleja responsabilidad en la administración del dinero. Uso de herramientas digitales Las aplicaciones financieras confiables , las billeteras digitales y otros servicios generan registros que ayudan a comprender mejor la actividad económica cotidiana. Comportamiento financiero El análisis de patrones relacionados con ingresos, gastos y organización financiera ofrece una visión más completa que la observación de movimientos aislados. Es importante destacar que cada entidad define los criterios que utiliza para sus procesos de evaluación y que la información debe tratarse siempre conforme a la normativa vigente sobre protección de datos. Cómo las fintech utilizan tecnología para entender mejor a los usuarios Las empresas fintech nacieron en un entorno completamente digital. Por esa razón han incorporado tecnologías avanzadas para comprender de forma más precisa las necesidades de sus usuarios. Inteligencia artificial Permite analizar grandes volúmenes de información en muy poco tiempo. Esto facilita identificar patrones de comportamiento financiero. Modelos automatizados Los sistemas pueden procesar información de manera eficiente y apoyar procesos de evaluación mucho más ágiles. Análisis de datos La integración de diferentes fuentes de información ayuda a construir perfiles financieros más completos. Actualización permanente Los modelos modernos pueden incorporar información reciente para reflejar mejor la realidad económica de los usuarios. Personalización Comprender mejor el comportamiento financiero permite desarrollar soluciones adaptadas a distintos perfiles y necesidades. Gracias a estas herramientas, las fintech han logrado ofrecer experiencias más rápidas, flexibles y centradas en las características particulares de cada usuario; ¡Eso es inclusión! Beneficios de ampliar las fuentes de información para evaluar oportunidades Complementar la evaluación financiera con nuevas fuentes de información ofrece ventajas tanto para las entidades como para los usuarios. Mayor inclusión financiera Personas con poca experiencia crediticia pueden contar con una evaluación más amplia de su comportamiento financiero. Comprensión más completa El análisis considera la evolución de los hábitos financieros y no únicamente algunos indicadores históricos. Evaluaciones más actualizadas La incorporación de información reciente permite reflejar mejor la situación económica actual de cada usuario. Procesos más eficientes La tecnología facilita el análisis de grandes volúmenes de información en tiempos reducidos. Productos más personalizados Comprender mejor el comportamiento financiero permite desarrollar soluciones adaptadas a diferentes necesidades. Impulso a la innovación Las nuevas metodologías favorecen el desarrollo de servicios financieros más modernos e inclusivos. Todo ello debe desarrollarse bajo principios de transparencia, protección de datos personales y uso responsable de la información. Cómo Monet utiliza modelos innovadores para impulsar la inclusión financiera La transformación digital ha permitido que plataformas como MONET desarrollen herramientas que complementan la evaluación financiera tradicional mediante el análisis responsable de diferentes indicadores relacionados con el comportamiento económico de sus usuarios. Este enfoque busca construir una visión más amplia del perfil financiero considerando aspectos como la actividad cotidiana, la organización de los movimientos financieros y otros patrones que ayudan a comprender mejor la realidad económica de cada persona. Para quienes apenas están comenzando su vida financiera, trabajan de forma independiente o cuentan con poca experiencia dentro del sistema crediticio tradicional, este tipo de innovación representa una oportunidad para que su comportamiento financiero pueda analizarse desde una perspectiva más completa. Incluso, la oportunidad se extiende también a personas que, por algún motivo, tienen la necesidad de un crédito estando reportadas en centrales de riesgo . La tecnología también facilita procesos más ágiles, experiencias digitales sencillas y una mejor capacidad para adaptarse a los cambios que experimentan las personas a lo largo del tiempo. Todo este proceso se desarrolla respetando principios de privacidad, seguridad y tratamiento responsable de los datos personales, elementos fundamentales para generar confianza dentro del ecosistema financiero. A medida que evolucionan los modelos de análisis, MONET continúa apostando por soluciones tecnológicas que contribuyan a ampliar la inclusión financiera y permitan comprender de forma más precisa las diferentes realidades económicas de los colombianos. Así que, sin tanto por pensar, ¡anímate a solicitar un crédito online! Preguntas frecuentes ¿Qué es el scoring invisible? Es un modelo de evaluación que complementa los criterios tradicionales utilizando información relacionada con el comportamiento financiero cotidiano para construir una visión más amplia del perfil económico de una persona. ¿El scoring invisible reemplaza el historial crediticio? No. Funciona como un complemento que aporta información adicional para enriquecer los procesos de evaluación financiera. ¿Qué tipo de información puede analizar un modelo alternativo? Dependiendo de cada entidad, puede considerar aspectos como la actividad transaccional, la regularidad de ingresos, los hábitos financieros y el uso de herramientas digitales, siempre respetando la normativa sobre protección de datos. ¿Por qué las fintech utilizan este tipo de modelos? Porque les permite comprender mejor la realidad financiera de diferentes perfiles de usuarios y desarrollar soluciones más inclusivas, ágiles y adaptadas a las nuevas dinámicas económicas. En conclusión: El acceso a los servicios financieros está evolucionando junto con la economía digital. El scoring invisible complementa la evaluación crediticia tradicional al incorporar diferentes señales sobre el comportamiento financiero, ofreciendo una visión más amplia, actualizada y cercana a la realidad de cada persona. Este enfoque favorece la inclusión financiera, especialmente para quienes están construyendo su historial o trabajan bajo modelos no tradicionales, al tiempo que permite desarrollar procesos más ágiles y productos más personalizados. Plataformas como MONET aprovechan estas innovaciones para crear modelos de análisis más completos y adaptados a las necesidades de los colombianos.

title: Introducing Lifecycle Studio: Go from idea to personalized campaigns, in minutes.
summary: For a decade, one lifecycle campaign meant 50 steps and weeks of waiting. That changes today.
body_text: When Anthropic dropped Claude Code, software engineering had a permanent redefining moment. The breakthrough was that engineers finally had a harness that understood how their work actually gets done. One that could navigate codebases, use tools, learn from context, and help move projects from idea to production. We believe marketing is next. The future of marketing will be defined with software that deeply understands a marketing discipline and can help teams accomplish real work from start to finish. Software that acts more like an agency than a platform, where you define the business goal and the system helps get it done. Reliably, on-brand, and grounded in your data. Today, we're launching Lifecycle Studio to give lifecycle and CRM teams that capability, reinventing what it means to run lifecycle marketing. The lifecycle workflow hasn't changed in a decade Every lifecycle marketer knows the process. An idea comes up. Someone writes a brief. Data science pulls the audience. Creative gets a request. Copy goes through review. Design builds the email. Ops assembles the journey. QA runs the checks. Four to six weeks later, the campaign finally launches. Workflows can’t keep up with your campaign ideas. Over the last decade, marketing technology made individual steps more efficient. Segmentation got faster. Content blocks became more dynamic. Journey builders became easier to use. But the workflow itself stayed mostly the same. The best ideas still wait in queues. Campaigns still depend on half a dozen handoffs. Teams still choose between speed, personalization, and quality because they rarely have the capacity to do all three. Lifecycle Studio reinvents the way marketing teams work Lifecycle Studio frees marketers to go from an idea to fully-built, personalized campaigns, in minutes. Marketers set the campaign goal, and agents draft the campaign brief, recommend audiences, generate content and creative, configure journeys, and prepare messages for activation—all grounded in the full context of your customer data, brand guidelines, creative history, campaign performance, and marketing stack. With Lifecycle Studio, marketing teams can now self-serve on the work that used to require a half-dozen dependencies without filing a single cross-team request. Thumbtack cut campaign cycles from six weeks to days, reduced cross-team effort by 75%, and launched programs they simply couldn't run before. The campaigns you've always wanted to run Most lifecycle teams are not short on ideas. They are short on the time, resources, and cross-functional bandwidth to actually get those ideas into market. Lifecycle Studio is built to help teams launch more campaigns, faster, without sacrificing quality or personalization. Here are a few ways marketers are using it today: Ship your full backlog. Every lifecycle team has campaigns they know are worth running but never quite get to: new onboarding tests, winback ideas, loyalty moments, better cross-sell journeys. Lifecycle Studio gives teams the capacity to finally move those ideas out of the queue and into market. Optimize the campaigns already running. The work does not stop once a journey is live. Teams still need new variants, better segments, refreshed copy, and more ways to improve performance. Lifecycle Studio makes it easier to keep improving live campaigns without turning every iteration into a new cross-functional project. Launch in the moments that matter. Sometimes the best campaign ideas are driven by moments. A sporting event, cultural viral trend, or breaking news. Lifecycle Studio helps teams move while the moment still matters, compressing the time from idea to live campaign from weeks to minutes. Turn market signals into campaigns. Instead of waiting for teams to find every opportunity manually, agents proactively surface opportunities and turn them into ready-to-launch campaigns. The result is a workflow where marketers are not just executing more ideas, they are discovering more of the right ones. “In just three months, we've moved dozens of strategies off the sticky note pile and into market. And my favorite part? The pile hasn't gotten smaller; it's gotten bigger. Because when execution catches up with ideas, you stop suppressing your ambitions to match capacity and start thinking bigger.” Lindsey Allison Director of Consumer Marketing at Fullspan Health What Lifecycle Studio does Lifecycle Studio operates a series of agents with access to your customer data, brand context, creative assets, and marketing stack. These agents help teams move from planning to launch without the traditional handoffs. Ideation. Agents draft briefs with audience segment recommendations, journey strategies, and messaging angles grounded in your customer history and engagement signals. Marketers can prompt directly in Lifecycle Studio, through Claude or ChatGPT via MCP. You define your campaign goals and preferred channels, the agents do the heavy lifting. Generation . Agents build every message variant, pulling from your DAM, product catalog, and past campaign templates to generate on-brand content at scale. Brand guidelines, compliance checks, dark-mode rendering, and ESP-specific templating are all handled in the same pass. Generate on-brand, production ready campaigns. Orchestration. After marketers review, refine, and send off for final approval, agents activate across email, push, and SMS through the marketing stack you already have. Once a campaign is approved, activate through your existing ESPs. Measurement. Every campaign feeds the next one. Agents pull engagement, conversion, and revenue data from every send, surface the patterns worth acting on, and recommend the content to inform the next campaign. Agents surface patterns and unforseen opportunities to act upon. Not all agentic marketing tools are created equal Agents are only as smart as the context they can reach. For most agentic marketing tools, that context is a fraction of what your team actually knows. Hightouch has a unique set of capabilities to achieve agentic marketing end-to-end where other AI tools in your stack fall short. Our agents connect directly to your data warehouse without copying data, creating a governed, composable context layer that understands your entire marketing operation and builds memory with every campaign. That gives Lifecycle Studio four advantages. Complete access to your customer data. Agents connect directly to your data warehouse to access all of your campaign and customer data. All of your brand context. Lifecycle Studio connects to your DAMs, Figma files, brand guidelines, legal policies, past ESP templates, and campaign history to create high-quality, on-brand campaigns in the right format, ready to send. End-to-end, from idea to execution. Unlike standalone AI tools that stop at content generation or isolated optimization, Lifecycle Studio closes the full workflow from brief to segmentation to content assembly to decisioning. A loop that gets smarter. Lifecycle Studio closes the entire loop — from brief to delivery to learning — and makes every campaign a foundation for the next one. The system gets smarter the more you use it. That compounding advantage is something a point solution can never replicate. “For my entire career, I've seen teams struggle to share learnings and apply them across channels. What’s most exciting about Lifecycle Studio is that it can actually absorb context and learn from performance to make every campaign smarter.” Allison Bryant Sr. Lifecycle Marketing Manager at GlossGenius The future of marketing is here For years, lifecycle teams have had to shape their ambition around capacity. That all changes when marketers have agents that can understand customer data, brand context, creative history, campaign performance, and business goals, then help turn that context into campaigns ready for market. The marketers who win in this next era will not be the ones who simply use AI to move faster. They will be the ones who combine creativity, taste, and judgment with agents that can execute with precision and learn from every campaign. “There's never been a better time to be a marketer. This is the first technology I've seen that eliminates the countless steps and cycles required to launch a campaign. For the first time, teams can execute faster and more efficiently, using the complete context of all their customer data to deliver on-brand experiences in any channel.” Mary Aguililla Lifecycle Marketing Manager at Hatch Lifecycle Studio is the second studio in Hightouch's Agentic Marketing Platform, alongside Ad Studio. Together they extend our vision for AI-native marketing infrastructure across paid and owned channels. To learn more, visit our product page .

title: AI Agents for Compliance Teams: How to Own AI by Approving the Building Blocks
summary: How compliance can own AI agents through grounding, approval, and audit, by approving the building blocks once.
body_text: Compliance is usually the team that slows AI down. With the right agent builder it becomes the team that ships it. The shift is moving governance upstream: compliance approves the building blocks once, and operators compose agents inside the rails. The agent grounds answers in approved data, routes the outputs that matter through named-owner sign-off, and writes an audit trail compliance can replay. Done that way, governance is a buyer rather than a blocker. Why per-output review makes compliance the bottleneck When the only control is reviewing each AI output, compliance becomes the constraint on every workflow. That works for a handful of outputs and breaks at scale, turning either into a queue that kills the time savings or a rubber stamp that defeats the purpose. The problem is the layer: review applied to each output cannot scale with the volume an agent produces. Move the review to the catalog. Decide once which sources an agent may read, which actions it may take, which channels it may use. Now every agent built from the catalog is in bounds by construction, and compliance spends its effort on the catalog rather than on each message. What compliance owns in this model The approved sources, actions, and channels that make up the catalog. Which outputs require named-owner sign-off before they land. The audit trail and the evidence it produces for auditors. The non-claim boundaries: what the agents must never do. Operators own composing agents from that catalog. The platform owns enforcement, keeping agents inside the rails, holding the approval gate, and writing the log. Nobody has to police every output by hand. Workflows that fit a compliance team itself Compliance is also a user, not only a gatekeeper. Agents that fit the team’s own work: Drafting suitability or policy documentation from a call or a case for responsible-owner sign-off. Screening against approved checklists and sanctions or watchlists, with a human confirming any match. Assembling audit-evidence packages from the trail. Answering staff policy questions with a citation to the approved source. Each keeps a person in the seat for the decision and removes the drafting and gathering around it. Evidence by default The audit trail is what makes compliance comfortable. Append-only, exportable, scoped per tenant, covering every question, source, draft, model call, and approval. When an auditor asks for a replay of a specific decision and proof the controls were on, the team produces it from the trail rather than opening a project. Where Clarm fits Clarm is built so compliance can approve the building blocks once and rely on the substrate to enforce them: grounding, approval, audit, and tenant isolation are invariants. title: Introducing CUB: Theta's Computer Use Benchmark
summary: Introducing CUB, a first-of-its-kind benchmark for computer and browser use agents with 106 end-to-end workflows across 7 industries.
body_text: Introducing CUB: Theta's Computer Use Benchmark 20% 15% 10% 5% 0% 9.2% 0.0% Manus 7.3% 0.0% OpenAI CUA 6.0% 0.0% Claude Computer Use * 3.8% 0.0% Browser Use * 0.6% 0.0% Gemini 2.5 Pro * Claude Computer Use: 3.7 Sonnet with thinking mode * Browser Use: with GPT-4o We're excited to announce CUB, a first-of-its-kind benchmark for computer and browser use agents. With 106 end-to-end workflows across consumer, construction, finance, healthcare, marketing, sales, and supply chain, CUB is the most diverse and representative benchmark for evaluating computer and browser use agents. We've worked with accountants, investment bankers, doctors, and other experts to create high-quality domain-specific tasks. These tasks involve real-world workflows and software tools across these industries, with synthetic versions of enterprise platforms such as SAP and CapIQ. We show an initial set of results below: After testing an initial set of five models and frameworks on the benchmark, we’ve found that leading solutions still struggle with computer use workflows. None of the agents were able to reach 10% on the benchmark—even with our granular evaluation system giving credit for partially correct solutions. In fact, there were less than 5 instances where an agent fully completed a task end-to-end. We developed this benchmark with a few key design choices in mind. Firstly, there is a significant gap of domain-specific evals for computer use agents. This is despite the fact that accounting, healthcare, finance, and other tasks are some of the most economically valuable work that agents are already being deployed for. Evaluating agents on end-to-end workflows is uniquely important because it requires agents to demonstrate proficiency in the following areas, each of which is critical in real-world tasks: Long-sequence memory and instruction following Coordination across multiple software applications Maintaining action coherence and reliability when performing repetitive tasks Interacting with unfamiliar and unintuitive domain-specific interfaces Alongside the benchmark, we’re also introducing our computer environment infrastructure for effective evaluation and post-training at scale. Optimized parallelization and VM snapshotting allows for faster evals and more data. Our environments support black-box agentic systems, a rich action space, and both browser and desktop-based configurations. We're looking forward to testing more models and frameworks on CUB. Please reach out to founders@thetasoftware.ai for more details. Some sample tasks are listed below. Example 1: Construction The agent is tasked with calculating the square footage of a property using publicly available block maps. In addition to navigating the website to find the correct block map, strong multimodal reasoning is required to understand the diagram and calculate the square footage. This task also critically tests long-sequence memory and intelligence, as the agent needs to understand that it has to navigate to previously seen pages for successful task completion. Example 2: Healthcare For this task, the agent is provided with a patient document from a recent eye exam and must enter pertinent information into an electronic health record (EHR) platform. The EHR navigation presents significant challenges beyond standard web interfaces due to hidden functionality and a complex interface. For example, entering data into the HPI Elements section requires identifying and activating a secondary interface panel not immediately visible within the examination record. The task also requires the agent to parse through significant amounts of information and demonstrate an advanced understanding of medical terminology.

How Animals Impact Our Electrical Infrastructure
summary: Wildlife and electrical infrastructure share the same space, and that relationship has an impact on electric reliability. Animals can cause outages by chewing on lines, building nests on equipment, or creating unintended electrical paths. body_text: Wildlife and electrical infrastructure share the same space, and that relationship has an impact on electric reliability. Animals can cause outages by chewing on lines, building nests on equipment, or creating unintended electrical paths. At Unitil, wildlife is responsible for roughly 13%* of power outages across our service territory, making it a common cause of service interruptions. Most animal-related outages occur in the spring and the fall when animals are most active. Why Squirrels and Birds Can Touch Power Lines You’ve probably seen a squirrel dart across a power line, or a row of birds settled comfortably on a wire. So why don’t they get shocked? It comes down to how electricity moves. Electrical current needs a complete path to flow from an energized source to the ground. When a squirrel or bird touches a single wire, that path isn’t completed. There’s no way for the current to get to the ground, so the animal isn’t impacted. People are a different story. In most cases, anyone who contacts an energized line will also be touching something grounded (a pole, a ladder, or the earth itself), completing the circuit through their body. To stay safe, always keep at least 10 feet away from overhead powerlines, and at least 30 feet away from downed power lines . If you see a downed line, report it to us immediately. When Wildlife Contact Causes Trouble Not every animal encounter with electrical equipment ends harmlessly. Animals that bridge two conductors at once, or contact both an energized line and a grounded surface, can cause outages and, unfortunately, serious harm to themselves. Squirrels are among the most frequent culprits, given the way they navigate across lines and equipment. Large birds, like raptors and herons, are especially vulnerable due to their wingspan relative to conductor spacing. Animals can also cause outages by chewing on lines and building nests on equipment. Even underground lines can be impacted. Burrowing animals like groundhogs and rodents can damage infrastructure over time, leading to outages that are more time consuming to repair. How We Work to Protect Both Service and Wildlife We take a proactive approach to keeping animal-related outages in check by using a variety of protective equipment designed to prevent animals from making contact with energized equipment. Transformer guards have sharp ends that deter squirrels from climbing on them. Diverters are a series of plastic baffles that direct birds and critters away from our wires and equipment. Utility pole caps deter wildlife from landing on top of poles while protecting the pole from moisture. In limited areas where nesting species are particularly active, we have utilized a different pole configuration to prevent nesting on equipment. These measures do double duty: they help maintain reliable service and reduce harm to wildlife. You Can Play a Role Too Set or move your feeders away from power lines. Avoid clearing dead trees in the spring and early summer while animals are nesting. Let us know if you spot unusual animal activity, like a large nest near power lines, utility poles, or other electrical equipment. Early reporting helps us respond quickly. Shared Space, Shared Responsibility Wildlife and electrical infrastructure will always coexist. We work to manage this relationship thoughtfully, keeping the lights on while being good stewards of the environment around us. Key Takeaways: Wildlife accounts for roughly 13%* of outages in Unitil’s service territory. Squirrels and birds can touch a single power line safely because they don’t complete an electrical circuit, but that protection doesn’t apply to people. Always keep your distance from power lines and never approach a downed wire. Unitil installs protective equipment like transformer guards and diverters to reduce animal-related outages. * Percentage based on 2021-2025 stats.

title: Branch Cuts DOI Inquiry Response Time by an Average of 70% With Kyber
summary: What once took Branch's Claims Compliance team days now takes hours with Kyber’s newest product launch.
body_text: The Stakeholder Branch is known for delivering fast, seamless claims experiences to its members. The claims organization consistently looks for ways to: Reduce administrative friction for adjusters Drive consistency and compliance in communications Improve responsiveness to policyholders As one of Kyber's earliest carrier partners, Branch has played an active role in shaping how the platform supports real-world workflows, including compliance use cases like DOI inquiry responses. “Addressing consumer inquiries is critical, but historically time-consuming,” said Ruth Deabold , Director of Claims Compliance & Operations at Branch. “Now, we focus on resolution instead of response-building, creating a faster, higher-quality experience with our team engaged at every step.” The Challenge A mandatory task that demands senior attention Department of Insurance (DOI) inquiry responses are a regulatory requirement every P&C insurer must handle. Each issue must be addressed directly, supporting documentation must be attached, and the tone must be professional. Most states require formal written responses within 10 to 30 calendar days, with no room for delays or incomplete submissions. Before Kyber, Branch's claims compliance team averaged three days to complete each response. The burden wasn't the volume. DOI inquiries don't arrive every day. But when they do, they demand immediate attention from the people best positioned to lead, not execute. Each response required: Assembling the full claim timeline and documentation Coordinating review across legal, compliance, and claims Formatting and finalizing the response under deadline pressure This work distracted the team from more strategic initiatives, taking days away and leading to bursts of reactive effort. The Breakthrough The first product of its kind At the time of launch, no carrier had access to a dedicated, production-grade AI solution built specifically for DOI inquiry responses. Compliance teams across the industry were still relying on manual workflows, static templates, and senior subject matter experts to assemble regulatory responses under deadline. While generative AI tools were emerging, none were structured to meet the documentation standards, allegation-by-allegation formatting, and audit traceability required for DOI submissions. Branch identified the gap and brought the opportunity directly to Kyber. Rather than adapting a generic drafting tool, the two teams co-developed a purpose-built DOI Inquiry Response AI Template designed around real compliance workflows. Together, they pressure-tested outputs against live inquiries, refined narrative structure, ensured documentation alignment, and embedded version control safeguards. The result was the first carrier-grade AI workflow of its kind. Built specifically for DOI responses, validated in production, and proven to reduce turnaround time by an average of 70% without sacrificing oversight or quality. AI-powered drafts with human oversight Branch implemented Kyber’s DOI Inquiry Response AI Template to streamline the team’s response workflow. As an existing Kyber user, they added the template to their growing set of AI-driven document use cases. Within their current compliance process, the team now generates expert-ready first drafts instead of building responses from scratch. Key elements of the implementation: Organized claim file summaries. Kyber pulls the full claim file record into a clear, organized summary of activity, making file reviews more efficient. Before going line by line, reviewers can see a quick summary of the entire claim file, saving time and surfacing key details faster. AI-generated first drafts . Kyber assembles the baseline response using claim data and documentation, eliminating hours of formatting and restating known facts. Human-in-the-loop review . Compliance professionals still review, revise, and approve every response before submission. Audit-ready tracking . Full version control and compliance notes from draft to delivery. Workflow integration . The AI works within Branch's existing systems rather than adding new tools or steps. The approach kept compliance firmly in control while removing the manual friction that consumed the most time.
