6 Best Outbound Dialers for Sales Automation in 2026
summary: Looking for the best outbound dialer? Compare Trellus, Orum, PhoneBurner, Five9, Convoso, and JustCall with pricing, pros, cons, and features.
body_text: Sales teams have never had more options when it comes to outbound dialers for sales automation . Some platforms connect calls quickly but leave long moments of silence before the rep starts speaking. Others pack in AI features but still expect sales teams to manually update CRMs after every conversation. A few protect your caller reputation well enough to keep answer rates healthy over time, while others burn through phone numbers surprisingly fast. To separate marketing claims from day to day performance, we evaluated eight leading platforms across real outbound environments instead of relying on demo accounts or vendor benchmarks. Across fourteen weeks of testing, we placed more than 62,000 outbound calls through B2B SaaS, health insurance, and solar lead generation campaigns. Every platform was measured against the same criteria, including connect rates, latency, CRM synchronization, compliance safeguards, abandoned call percentages, and total operating cost. One lesson became obvious very quickly. Dialing more numbers rarely solves pipeline problems. Winning outbound teams rely on software that protects caller reputation, keeps every campaign compliant, removes repetitive admin work, and helps representatives spend more time speaking with qualified prospects. Here are the platforms that delivered the strongest overall performance. 1. Trellus: Best Overall Outbound Dialer for Sales Automation What does it do? Trellus combines AI assisted dialing, parallel calling, real time coaching, CRM synchronization, and LinkedIn prospecting inside a single outbound workspace. Rather than acting as another standalone dialer, it becomes the operating system sales reps spend most of their day inside. Who is it for? B2B sales teams, SDR organizations, agencies, and revenue leaders looking to increase conversation volume while giving representatives live coaching, AI assistance, and workflow automation without stitching together multiple platforms. During testing, this platform consistently delivered one of the smoothest calling experiences across every campaign. Reps moved between calls with almost no downtime, AI coaching surfaced relevant guidance while conversations were still happening, and CRM updates happened automatically after each interaction. That combination produced something far more valuable than simply increasing call volume. Representatives stayed in selling mode throughout the day. There was very little context switching between browser tabs, spreadsheets, CRM records, LinkedIn research, and separate coaching software. Managers could monitor conversations in real time, identify coaching opportunities immediately, and help newer SDRs improve without waiting until the end of the week to review recordings. The platform also proved particularly useful for remote sales organizations where managers cannot physically walk the sales floor. Live coaching prompts, conversation insights, and workflow automation kept performance much more consistent across the entire team. Compared to traditional power dialer software , productivity gains came from reducing administrative work just as much as increasing call volume. Pros AI powered live coaching during active sales conversations. Parallel dialing dramatically increases conversations per hour. Native CRM synchronization eliminates manual call logging. Built in LinkedIn workflow support keeps prospect research close to the dialing experience. Fast connection times create natural conversations with minimal dead air. Excellent value compared with buying multiple standalone sales tools. Cons Teams coming from traditional dialers may need several days to adapt to the AI assisted workflow. Organizations that only need basic calling may not take advantage of the broader feature set. Pricing We offer multi tier pricing plans to fit every sales first business’s requirement. Why it ranks first Many outbound products solve one piece of the workflow. Some specialize in dialing speed. Others concentrate on coaching. Others focus on CRM updates. This platform brings those capabilities together into a single workflow, which reduces operational complexity while helping sales teams generate more pipeline. For companies looking for outbound call automation without creating another disconnected sales tool stack, it provides one of the strongest overall combinations of productivity, coaching, automation, and scalability available today. 2. Orum: Best Parallel Dialer for High Volume SDR Teams What does it do? Orum is a parallel dialer built for outbound sales organizations that care about one metric above almost everything else, live conversations per hour. Rather than calling one prospect at a time, the platform dials multiple numbers simultaneously and only connects the representative once a real person answers. Who is it for? Mid sized and enterprise SDR teams with ten or more representatives that spend most of the day cold calling B2B prospects and want to maximize conversation volume without hiring additional reps. If someone asked me to recommend a predictive dialer for sales teams that prioritizes speed above everything else, Orum would be one of the first platforms that comes to mind. During testing, I deployed the Launch plan across an eight person SaaS SDR team selling into IT leaders . Prior to introducing Orum, each rep averaged roughly nine live conversations every hour while manually dialing through prospect lists. That number changed dramatically after switching to parallel dialing. Conversation volume climbed to approximately forty two live conversations per hour per representative. That lines up closely with the company's published benchmarks and demonstrates why parallel dialing continues to attract high growth outbound teams. The productivity improvement wasn't simply about dialing more numbers. Representatives stopped waiting between calls, voicemail became far less disruptive, and the platform handled repetitive actions automatically. Throughout a typical workday, that saved hours that would have been spent listening to ringing phones and leaving identical voicemail messages. Managers also benefited from the built in virtual sales floor. Rather than reviewing recordings several days later, they could jump into active conversations, coach representatives while momentum was still high, and identify patterns across the team much faster. Those capabilities make Orum one of the strongest options for companies searching for outbound dialers for sales automation where conversation volume directly impacts pipeline generation. That said, the platform is not without tradeoffs. The biggest issue I encountered appeared during the handoff between the prospect answering and the representative joining the call. Across approximately 2,100 answered conversations, there was frequently a one to two second bridge delay before the SDR could begin speaking. Many prospects answered the phone, heard silence, then immediately responded with "Hello? Hello?" before disconnecting. Around eighteen percent of answered calls ended before the representative even delivered an opening sentence. Those dropped conversations add up quickly across thousands of dials and partially offset the productivity gains created through parallel calling. Data quality also becomes far more important with Orum than many buyers initially expect. The company publishes pickup rates around 5.3 percent, which means poor prospect lists can burn through caller IDs surprisingly fast. Running large amounts of low quality data through five simultaneous lines accelerates number reputation problems much faster than traditional single line dialing. For organizations that already maintain clean prospect databases, the platform performs considerably better. Pros Five to ten simultaneous dialing lines generated a genuine four to five times increase in live conversations compared with manual dialing. The virtual sales floor gave managers the ability to listen, coach, and review active calls without waiting for recordings after the workday ended. AI powered voicemail detection and phone tree navigation removed much of the repetitive downtime that slows outbound prospecting. Native Salesforce and Outreach integrations automatically synchronized call outcomes, helping representatives stay focused on selling instead of updating records. Cons One to two second bridge delays occasionally produced awkward openings, contributing to roughly eighteen percent of answered calls ending before representatives could begin speaking. Pricing starts at $250 per user each month with annual billing and a three seat minimum, creating a fairly high entry point for smaller sales organizations. Calling is still the primary workflow, meaning companies will likely need separate software for email sequencing, prospect data, and CRM management. The Ascend plan requires custom pricing and can reach several hundred dollars per user each month depending on deployment size. Pricing Launch starts at $250 per user per month with annual billing and a three seat minimum. Ascend is custom priced and commonly ranges between $400 and $500 or more per user each month , depending on deployment size and international calling requirements. Implementation services frequently add another $1,000 to $5,000 as a one time cost. Bottom line Orum earns its reputation because it solves one problem exceptionally well. It helps SDRs speak with far more prospects during a normal workday. If your outbound strategy revolves around maximizing conversation volume, it remains one of the strongest auto dialer software options available today. Companies looking for a complete sales call center software platform with built in email automation, richer multichannel engagement, or AI agents capable of handling conversations autonomously may find themselves adding several complementary tools around it. That extra software increases overall cost, but for outbound teams where every additional conversation can produce more qualified meetings, many revenue leaders consider that investment worthwhile. Predictive Dialer vs Power Dialer: Which Is Better for Sales Teams? One question comes up almost every time companies begin evaluating outbound dialers for sales automation . Should you choose a predictive dialer or a power dialer? The answer depends less on company size and far more on how your sales organization operates each day. A predictive dialer calls multiple prospects before an agent becomes available. Once someone answers, the system routes that live conversation to the next available representative. This approach works extremely well inside high volume call centers where efficiency and conversation volume matter more than personalization. Power dialers work differently. They place one call immediately after another without asking representatives to manually initiate every conversation. The rep stays in complete control of each interaction while eliminating the downtime that normally exists between calls. Teams selling complex B2B products often prefer power dialers because representatives have a few seconds to review account information before speaking. High volume lead generation teams usually lean toward predictive or parallel dialing because maximizing conversations has a larger impact on revenue than spending extra preparation time before every call. There isn't one universal winner. The better choice depends on your sales motion, your compliance requirements, your average deal value, and how personalized each conversation needs to be. 3. PhoneBurner: Best Single Line Power Dialer for B2B Sales What does it do? PhoneBurner is a cloud based power dialer software designed to eliminate the downtime between outbound calls. It keeps representatives moving from one conversation to the next without introducing the bridge delays that sometimes appear with parallel dialing platforms. Who is it for? Small and mid market B2B sales teams, financial services firms, agencies, and inside sales organizations that value high quality conversations more than dialing as many numbers as possible every hour. PhoneBurner approaches outbound calling very differently from parallel dialers. Rather than placing five or ten calls simultaneously, it concentrates on making every live connection feel natural from the moment the prospect answers. That difference became obvious during testing. I rolled the platform out to a five representative financial services team calling pre qualified mortgage leads over a six week period. Before introducing the software, each rep averaged around twenty conversations per hour through manual dialing. After deployment, representatives consistently reached between seventy eight and eighty two contacts every hour. That productivity gain was impressive on its own. The larger improvement came from the quality of the conversations. Unlike several parallel dialers that introduce a noticeable pause before the representative joins the call, PhoneBurner bridges prospects almost instantly. A short bridge announcement plays while the representative reviews the contact record, giving them enough time to personalize their opening without forcing the prospect to sit through uncomfortable silence. It sounds like a small design decision. During thousands of outbound conversations, those extra couple of seconds made calls feel considerably more natural. Prospects were far more likely to remain engaged because they immediately heard a confident introduction rather than wondering if someone had accidentally called them. Another area where PhoneBurner performed well was caller reputation. Across more than twelve thousand outbound calls, ARMOR spam protection kept our numbers off spam labeling services throughout the entire testing period. That helped maintain stable answer rates, something many companies overlook when evaluating outbound call automation platforms. A dialer that delivers high call volume loses much of its value if recipients stop answering because your numbers are flagged as spam. The platform also simplified administrative work. Calls, voicemails, emails, SMS activity, and dispositions synchronized automatically across CRM platforms, allowing representatives to move directly into the next conversation without spending several minutes updating records. For companies researching the best outbound dialers with CRM integration for sales automation , PhoneBurner remains one of the strongest choices in the mid market. Pros Zero connection delay created natural conversations and eliminated the awkward silence commonly associated with many parallel dialers. ARMOR spam protection and Connect Scores helped maintain healthy caller reputation across more than twelve thousand outbound calls. Built in CRM capabilities along with more than 150 integrations automatically logged calls, voicemail drops, emails, and SMS activity. Unlimited dialing with no additional per minute charges makes budgeting straightforward for outbound teams placing large call volumes. Representatives can review contact information before speaking, leading to more personalized introductions and stronger first impressions. Cons Pricing ranges from approximately $149 to $165 per representative each month, making it a significant investment for smaller teams. International dialing is unavailable, limiting adoption for organizations selling outside the United States and Canada. The sixty minute trial provides limited opportunity to stress test the platform under real campaign conditions. Inbound functionality and more advanced SMS capabilities require the Premium plan, increasing total subscription costs. Pricing Standard starts at $165 per user each month , or approximately $140 with annual billing . Professional costs $195 per user monthly , or around $165 annually . Premium starts at $215 per representative each month , or roughly $183 with annual billing . Bottom line PhoneBurner remains one of the strongest auto dialer software platforms for sales organizations that believe conversation quality matters just as much as conversation volume. Representatives spend less time waiting between calls, managers spend less time cleaning CRM data, and prospects experience a smoother interaction from the moment they answer the phone. Companies searching for sales call center software built specifically around outbound prospecting will appreciate its reliability, ease of deployment, and mature CRM ecosystem. Organizations running global sales teams or looking for extensive multichannel outreach may eventually outgrow its capabilities, but for North American outbound teams it continues to be one of the most dependable options available. What Is an Outbound Dialer and How Does It Work for Sales Automation? This is one of the most common questions revenue leaders ask after seeing modern outbound platforms in action. At a basic level, an outbound dialer automates the repetitive work involved in placing sales calls. Without one, representatives manually search for contact records, dial phone numbers, wait through ringing, listen to voicemail greetings, leave messages, update the CRM, then repeat the process hundreds of times throughout the day. Only a small portion of that workflow involves speaking with prospects. Everything else is administrative overhead. Modern outbound dialers for sales automation remove much of that repetitive work. The software automatically places calls, detects answering machines, skips disconnected numbers, records outcomes, updates CRM records, schedules follow ups, and routes representatives directly to live prospects whenever possible. The amount of automation depends on the type of dialer. A power dialer places one call immediately after another, helping representatives maintain momentum without manually dialing every contact. A predictive dialer analyzes agent availability and places multiple calls ahead of time, connecting representatives only when someone answers. Parallel dialers push that concept even further, dialing several numbers simultaneously to maximize live conversations. Many modern platforms also include AI capabilities. These systems can summarize conversations, recommend coaching tips during live calls, generate follow up emails, update CRM fields automatically, and in some cases even conduct conversations without a human representative participating. 4. Five9: Best Enterprise Predictive Dialer for 50 Plus Seat Contact Centers What does it do? Five9 is an enterprise grade cloud contact center platform that combines predictive, progressive, preview, and power dialing with workforce management, IVR, AI assistance, analytics, and inbound support. It is built for organizations that want most of their customer communication tools inside one platform. Who is it for? Large contact centers, insurance providers, financial institutions, healthcare organizations, and enterprise sales teams operating with fifty or more agents. Five9 has been part of the contact center market for years, and after spending several weeks running live campaigns through it, it became clear why so many enterprise organizations continue to rely on the platform. Its biggest strength is maturity. Many newer AI platforms specialize in outbound prospecting, while Five9 attempts to cover nearly every communication workflow inside a large organization. During testing, I deployed the platform across a fifty two seat insurance contact center handling both inbound claims and outbound policy renewal campaigns. That environment created a much tougher workload than a typical SDR team. Agents were constantly moving between inbound customer conversations and outbound renewal calls, making pacing accuracy far more important than raw dialing speed. The predictive dialer handled that balancing act surprisingly well. Across thirty consecutive days, abandoned calls stayed around 2.4 percent, comfortably below the FTC safe harbor threshold of three percent. That pacing reduced compliance concerns while still keeping representatives consistently busy throughout the day. Another feature that stood out was AI Agent Assist. Rather than forcing agents to write detailed summaries after every conversation, the platform generated call notes automatically and suggested follow up actions before the next interaction even started. Across hundreds of daily conversations, that reduced post call work by roughly forty seconds per call. Forty seconds may not sound significant. Multiply that across thousands of customer interactions every month and the productivity gains become substantial. For enterprise organizations evaluating predictive dialer for sales teams operating at scale, these operational efficiencies can translate into thousands of additional selling hours each year. Where Five9 became less attractive was cost. The advertised subscription pricing only tells part of the story. Smaller companies should pay close attention to those additional expenses before making a decision. Pros Predictive, progressive, preview, and power dialing are all available inside one enterprise platform, giving managers flexibility across different campaign types. Intelligent pacing kept abandoned call rates below the FTC three percent guideline throughout our month long evaluation. AI Agent Assist generated summaries, recommendations, and call notes automatically, reducing post call administrative work. Enterprise security features include SSO, HIPAA support, PCI DSS compliance, SRTP encryption, and detailed role based permissions. Five nines uptime performed exactly as advertised during testing, with no noticeable voice outages across the deployment. Cons Public pricing only covers the entry level plans, while many enterprise features require separate quotes from the sales team. The recommended deployment begins at approximately fifty seats, making it difficult for growing businesses to justify. CRM integrations with Salesforce, ServiceNow, Zendesk, and other platforms often carry additional licensing costs. Full implementation commonly takes between six and twelve weeks, considerably longer than many AI native outbound platforms. Pricing Digital starts around $119 per user each month . Core starts around $159 per user each month . Premium, Optimum, and Ultimate require custom enterprise quotes. Most organizations receive the strongest pricing under thirty six month agreements with approximately fifty seats or more. Bottom line Five9 remains one of the strongest choices for enterprise organizations searching for comprehensive sales call center software rather than a standalone outbound dialer. Its compliance controls, predictive pacing, security certifications, and blended communication capabilities make it particularly attractive for regulated industries where reliability carries more weight than maximizing outbound conversations alone. Growing SaaS companies with smaller sales teams may find lighter AI driven platforms easier to deploy and considerably less expensive. 5. Convoso: Best Compliance Heavy Dialer for Lead Generation What does it do? Convoso is an outbound contact center platform built around high volume calling. It combines predictive, progressive, preview, power, and manual dialing with reputation management, compliance controls, lead distribution, and reporting tools designed for industries that place thousands of outbound calls every day. Who is it for? Insurance agencies, solar companies, lead generation firms, BPOs, financial services organizations, and sales teams where compliance carries as much importance as call volume. Some outbound platforms win because they produce more conversations. Convoso earns its place for a different reason. It helps organizations keep those conversations compliant. That becomes increasingly valuable as outbound regulations continue becoming more complex across different states and industries. I tested Convoso during a fourteen day solar lead generation campaign involving twenty five agents calling purchased prospect lists supplied through four different vendors. Purchased lists usually expose weaknesses in dialing platforms very quickly. Caller reputation drops faster, spam labeling becomes more common, and poor data quality increases compliance risk. Convoso handled those conditions reasonably well. Dynamic caller ID rotation maintained answer rates between roughly 7.1 percent and 8.4 percent throughout the testing period, keeping performance close to the team's historical averages despite the inconsistent quality of the underlying data. The reputation management dashboard proved particularly useful. On the sixth day of testing, two outbound numbers were identified as receiving spam labels. The compliance features impressed me even more. Automatic Do Not Call scrubbing, state specific calling windows, and built in Florida Telephone Solicitation Act settings all operated without requiring constant supervision. For organizations placing hundreds of thousands of outbound calls every month, those safeguards reduce both administrative work and legal exposure. The platform does demand a greater time investment during implementation. Compared with simpler cloud dialers, administrators need a deeper understanding of campaign configuration before everything begins running smoothly. Organizations with experienced operations teams usually adapt quickly. Smaller companies without dedicated administrators may find the learning curve steeper. Pros Predictive, progressive, preview, manual, and power dialing are available inside one platform, giving managers flexibility across different campaign types. Reputation management automatically rotates flagged caller IDs before declining answer rates begin affecting campaign performance. Automatic Do Not Call scrubbing and state specific calling windows reduce compliance work considerably. Answering machine detection kept representative idle time below eight percent during predictive dialing campaigns. Built for industries handling large outbound volumes where compliance requirements are part of everyday operations. Cons Pricing is custom quoted, making budgeting more difficult before speaking with the sales team. Free trial availability generally starts around forty seats, limiting accessibility for smaller businesses. Initial configuration commonly takes two to three weeks before administrators become comfortable managing campaigns independently. The administrative interface requires more training than several newer cloud based competitors. Pricing Pricing typically starts around $90 per user each month , based on industry estimates and deployment size. Final costs depend on seat count, telephony requirements, feature selection, and contract length. Carrier fees are billed separately. Bottom line Convoso shines when compliance sits near the top of the buying criteria. Companies operating in insurance, solar, healthcare, financial services, and outsourced lead generation often face regulations that leave very little room for error. Its combination of reputation management, compliance automation, flexible dialing modes, and campaign controls makes it one of the stronger sales call center software solutions for organizations handling large outbound operations. 6. JustCall: Best Mid Market Dialer Under $100 Per Seat What does it do? JustCall combines cloud telephony, outbound dialing, SMS, WhatsApp messaging, AI transcription, and CRM synchronization into one affordable communications platform. It offers power dialing, predictive dialing, and dynamic dialing capabilities without enterprise level pricing. Who is it for? Sales teams, customer success departments, recruiting firms, agencies, and growing businesses with approximately five to thirty representatives looking for a capable outbound platform without stretching the software budget. JustCall occupies an interesting position in the market. Many platforms force buyers into one of two categories. You either purchase an expensive enterprise contact center platform or settle for a basic business phone system with limited automation. JustCall sits comfortably between those extremes. I evaluated the Pro plan across a twelve representative SaaS sales team targeting mid market businesses over a three week period. Deployment took less than a day, making it one of the quickest implementations among all the platforms tested. Representatives averaged approximately sixty two successful prospect conversations per day while the built in Sales Dialer handled repetitive dialing tasks automatically. The productivity improvement came from more than dialing speed. Every conversation synchronized directly with HubSpot, complete with transcripts, dispositions, recordings, and notes. Before moving to JustCall, representatives spent several minutes updating CRM records after nearly every conversation. Those manual updates disappeared almost entirely. Over several weeks, that translated into meaningful time savings across the entire team. There are a few limitations worth considering before making a purchase. HIPAA compliance is reserved for higher tier enterprise plans with minimum license requirements, limiting adoption for smaller healthcare organizations. The unlimited calling policy also includes fair usage limits. During testing, accounts exceeding approximately forty two hundred minutes per representative during a month triggered additional usage review and overage charges. Heavy outbound teams should keep that policy in mind before assuming unlimited means unrestricted. Pros Competitive pricing makes advanced dialing features accessible to growing sales organizations. Strong HubSpot and Salesforce integrations automatically synchronize calls, recordings, transcripts, and dispositions. SMS, WhatsApp, voice, and AI transcription work together inside one communication platform. Fourteen day trial provides enough time to evaluate the software during live campaigns. AI Voice Agent offers an entry point for businesses beginning to experiment with conversational AI. Cons Sales Dialer requires the Pro subscription, while lower priced plans include only basic calling functionality. Fair usage limits may trigger additional charges for organizations placing extremely high outbound call volumes. HIPAA support requires enterprise licensing with minimum seat commitments. AI Voice Agent usage is billed separately from the core subscription. Pricing Team starts at $29 per user each month . Pro starts at $49 per user each month , which includes the Sales Dialer. Pro Plus starts at $89 per user each month . Business pricing is available through custom quotes with minimum licensing requirements. Bottom line JustCall delivers an impressive balance between features, usability, and affordability. Growing companies searching for reliable auto dialer software without enterprise pricing will find plenty to like here. It offers enough automation to improve productivity, enough CRM connectivity to eliminate repetitive administration, and enough communication channels to support modern outbound prospecting without forcing buyers into six figure annual software commitments. How We Evaluated These Outbound Dialer Platforms? There is no shortage of software comparison articles that rank products based on feature lists alone. That approach rarely tells you what it feels like to run an outbound team every day. Two platforms can both advertise AI coaching, CRM integrations, predictive dialing, and compliance features, yet produce completely different experiences once hundreds or thousands of calls start flowing through the system. That is why our evaluation concentrated on day to day operational performance rather than marketing checklists. Across fourteen weeks, we measured how each platform behaved under live campaign conditions. The testing covered B2B SaaS prospecting, health insurance outreach, and solar lead generation, giving us exposure to very different calling environments. Every platform was scored across six major categories. 1. Dialing speed and automation The first thing we wanted to understand was how efficiently each platform moved representatives from one live conversation to the next. Raw dialing speed tells only part of the story. Connection quality matters just as much. Some outbound dialers for sales automation can place several calls simultaneously, but if prospects hear silence before the representative joins, many conversations end before they even begin. During testing, we measured several performance indicators, including: Average time between one completed call and the next outbound attempt. Live answer detection accuracy. Voicemail detection reliability. Bridge latency between prospect pickup and representative connection. Average live conversations generated per hour. Platforms that connected representatives almost immediately after a prospect answered consistently delivered stronger customer experiences. Those introducing noticeable delays lost points because even a one or two second pause can reduce engagement and increase abandoned conversations. We also evaluated how well each platform automated repetitive dialing tasks without requiring representatives to intervene throughout the day. 2. AI capabilities and automation depth AI appears in almost every software demo today. The quality of that AI varies dramatically. Some platforms simply generate transcripts after conversations finish. Others actively support representatives while calls are taking place. The strongest platforms went considerably further. They provided real time coaching, summarized conversations automatically, updated CRM records, generated follow up activities, surfaced objection handling guidance, and reduced administrative work without interrupting the representative's workflow. We also considered an increasingly important question. Can the software conduct conversations on its own? Several vendors continue positioning AI as an assistant sitting beside human representatives. Newer platforms have begun introducing conversational AI agents capable of qualifying leads, booking appointments, answering questions, and handling portions of outbound prospecting independently. As outbound call automation continues evolving, those capabilities will play a much larger role in software purchasing decisions. 3. Multichannel engagement Cold calling rarely succeeds through one conversation alone. Many prospects answer after receiving an email. Others respond after seeing a text message. Some return calls after multiple touchpoints spread across several days. That makes multichannel engagement an important part of modern outbound prospecting. We looked closely at how each platform handled communication beyond voice. Areas included: SMS automation. Email follow up. WhatsApp messaging. Automated voicemail drops. Sequencing workflows. Follow up scheduling. Platforms offering several communication channels inside one environment received stronger scores because they reduced the need for separate software subscriptions. Businesses looking for complete sales call center software increasingly expect these capabilities as standard functionality rather than premium add ons.

title: Understanding Key Changes to NSIP Guidance Updates
summary: Major updates to national infrastructure planning guidance are bringing greater programme flexibility while maintaining an emphasis on proportionality and early issue-setting in the development consent order (DCO) process.
body_text: Major updates to national infrastructure planning guidance are bringing greater programme flexibility while maintaining an emphasis on proportionality and early issue-setting in the development consent order (DCO) process. The Ministry of Housing, Communities and Local Government recently published updates to much of the guidance for nationally significant infrastructure projects (NSIPs) through its National Infrastructure Guidance Portal. The updates to this guidance confirm the intention for real change to the development consent order (DCO) regime, based on the reforms set out in the Planning and Infrastructure Act. Most significantly, guidance relating to the removal of the statutory duty to consult allows applicants greater flexibility in defining their approach. Statements of Community Consultation (SoCCs), Preliminary Environmental Information Reports (PEIRs) and Consultation Reports are no longer required. In this article we explore the key changes and what they mean for developers. While the updates demonstrate a real appetite for change, the sheer scale of these take a lot to digest. In this article our team has done some of the hard work, summarising the key changes and their impact on developers. What are the key takeaways from the NSIP guidance updates? Greater flexibility on the timing and approach to consultation and engagement, and the statutory requirement for consultation has been removed The corresponding removal of the requirement for a SoCC, PEIR or consultation report There is a strong focus on appropriate, proportionate, and targeted consultation and engagement, as well as the early identification of issues, including use of the Initial Assessment of Principal Issues (IAPI) There is an emphasis on the proportionality of documents, focusing on key issues In practice, this means a faster pre-application stage and greater flexibility in pre-application programmes. Developers will need to identify a suitably tailored approach to consultation and engagement, and applicants will have a greater responsibility to deliver in line with the reformed regime. Below we have outlined some of the key changes to the guidance and what this will mean for applicants and their advisors. Is your project an NSIP? New guidance sets out details of how Section 35 of the Planning Act will be applied, directing projects into and out of the NSIP regime in line with the amendments made through the Planning and Infrastructure Act. Changes to the consultation process Following the removal of the statutory duty to consult under Sections 42, 43, 44, 45, 47 and 49 of the Planning Act, the guidance provides updates on the approach to consultation and engagement at the pre-application stage. It confirms that there is no longer a requirement for a SoCC to set out the approach to consultation, and the need for PEIRs and consultation reports is also removed. This means there is no longer any need to follow precedent to ensure the consultation is ‘adequate’. As ever, existing principles of good consultation continue to apply, but the guidance places the responsibility on applicants to determine how best to programme their project, the best approach to consultation, the appropriate material to accompany consultation, and who to consult. Consultation requirements under other regimes, in particular the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) Regulations, still apply, but these changes should allow greater emphasis on effective consultation on targeted issues. The challenge for applicants and their advisors is to be bold in adopting the reforms while ensuring strong, effective, targeted consultation. Done properly, this should significantly reduce pre-application timescales, inform good design and mitigation, and allow a focus on reducing the issues to be taken to examination. With the removal of the requirement for additional formal consultation, applicants also have the option to make design changes without being constrained by consultation timeframes. Appropriate timing of notification and publicising Sections 46 and 48 of the Planning Act remain, but appropriate timing for notifying the Secretary of State of the proposed application (Section 46) and publicising the application (Section 48) has been introduced, following the removal of Section 42 (statutory consultation). Applicants are encouraged to notify “as early as possible, and where practicable, not less than 6 months before submission of the DCO application”. Greater emphasis on Initial Assessment of Principal Issues (IAPI) Throughout the updated guidance, there is considerable emphasis on the role of the IAPI. It is recognised as a tool that can identify key issues and focus the examination process. Applicants should aim to use the pre-application stage to narrow areas of disagreement and address these where possible before submission of the application. This will help the Examining Authority in preparing the IAPI, enabling a more focused, proportionate and efficient examination. Inclusion of Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) statements The guidance confirms that, from 2 November 2026, applications must include an outline biodiversity gain statement. Applicants are encouraged to share indicative BNG requirements and their proposed approach to delivery with PINS and stakeholders during pre-application to inform development of the outline plan. Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) The guidance places continued emphasis on clarity, a proportional approach to EIA, and compliance with the scoping opinion. It also confirms the relevance of the Rochdale Envelope approach to identifying reasonable worst-case parameters where further detailed design or design flexibility is required. Acceptance The guidance on the acceptance stage has been updated, removing the requirement for consultation as a statutory consideration for acceptance, and reiterates the importance of: Consistency across application documents Complete, robust, and credible documents that accurately reflect the proposed development at submission Sufficiency in scale and content for the proposed development Concise, clearly written, and well-structured documents that are easy to navigate In conclusion, the updated guidance sets out four key principles: Prioritising front-loading : identification of key issues and the engagement and consultation on these Proportionality: a proportionate approach to preparing the application and to engagement and consultation Openness and transparency: applicants are encouraged to adopt these principles in any consultation and engagement, and explain what information is sought, where stakeholders can influence the project, and where they cannot Timeliness: applicants are encouraged to approach consultation and engagement in a timely and collaborative manner. Finally, we expect further updates and guidance to be published throughout 2026 and 2027 relating to several areas. These include: The fast-track process Changes to DCOs Compulsory acquisition The Infrastructure Planning (Fees) Regulations Award of costs Guidance on the process for reviewing the National Policy Statements A new section 55 checklist. Current understanding is that this will include matters of judgement rather than simply being a tick-box checklist. About the authors Amy Robinson Amy Robinson is a senior director in our EIA team and has more than 25 years’ experience in leading major infrastructure projects across a range of sectors, particularly transmission, solar, onshore andoffshore wind, battery storage and data centre clients. View bio Her experience includes EIA lead and project director roles for Gatwick Northern Runway, Morgan and Morecambe Transmission Assets, Ossian Offshore Wind Farm (Transmission Infrastructure), Hornsea Project One, Hornsea Project Three, Atlantic Array offshore wind farm, Botley West solar, Coalburn, Coalburn II and Devilla Forest BESS projects and the Generic Disposal Facility for radioactive waste. Camilla Fisher Camilla Fisher is a Technical Director in our national infrastructure planning team. View bio Camilla has more than 20 years’ experience in infrastructure projects, including providing consenting and programme advice on DCOs and other major infrastructure projects. Her major infrastructure experience includes acting as consenting lead for Mona Offshore Wind Project, Morgan Offshore Wind Project, Ossian Offshore Wind Farm (Transmission Infrastructure), the PHE Science Hub and confidential data centre and AWE projects. title: The Dark Side of Quviviq: Uncovering the Potential Side Effects
summary: Explore the potential side effects of Quviviq in our comprehensive guide. Uncover crucial insights for informed decisions on sleep medication.
body_text: People who experience insomnia may have encountered Quviviq as a possible solution. The medication functions through a distinct mechanism compared to traditional sleep medications. The brain's orexin system serves as the target for Quviviq to help people both fall asleep and maintain continuous sleep. The medication works for specific individuals but all drugs produce adverse reactions. The knowledge of expected side effects will assist you in determining whether this medication suits your needs. We asked Dr. Shiyan Yeo, Internal Medicine Physician and Sleep Medicine Expert, about potential side effects of Quviviq. She says: Quviviq is a newer sleep aid, but like all medications, it has potential side effects, from daytime drowsiness to vivid dreams. Ultimately, what she means is newer sleep medications can come with unwanted side effects too, making it important to discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor before starting treatment. Quviviq at a Glance Quviviq, a prescription medication, primarily targets the facilitation of sleep onset and maintenance for individuals with insomnia . Its active ingredient, daridorexant, acts on specific receptors within the brain. As with any pharmacological intervention, Quviviq embodies both therapeutic benefits and possible side effects . These effects range from mild to severe and may vary based on individual physiology and concurrent medication usage. The term “side effects” encompasses both the unintended reactions and tolerability profile of Quviviq when incorporated into a patient's sleep management regimen. What Is Quviviq? Quviviq, also known as daridorexant, is a medicine used to treat insomnia . The way it works is by calming down the signals in your brain that keep you awake and targets something called the orexin system which is the system that helps manage sleep and wake cycles in the body. Unlike other sleep medicines, it does not sedate you. Instead, it supports the natural process of falling asleep and staying asleep. Quviviq's Intended Benefits Quviviq is meant to: Help you fall asleep faster Reduce how often you wake up during the night Help you stay asleep for longer Improve how rested you feel in the morning Support better energy, mood, and focus during the day Common Physical Reactions Upon administration of Quviviq, individuals might encounter a range of physical side effects. These responses are consistent with the pharmacokinetics of a substance manipulating the orexin neurotransmitter system. Patients can experience symptoms such as headache, a common occurrence that emerges in the initial phase of treatment. Adverse effects might also include fatigue and dizziness, alterations signaling the central nervous system's adaptation to Quviviq. Less frequent, but worthy of note, are gastrointestinal disturbances like nausea or dry mouth, which manifest due to the drug's systemic activity. It is crucial for patients to monitor these reactions and communicate with healthcare providers about their severity and impact on daily functioning. Digestive Discomfort The medication can cause nausea together with dry mouth and constipation. Some users experience modifications in their bowel movements. The side effects remain mild but they can produce discomfort for some patients. Nausea - A prevalent side effect which may occur shortly after taking the medication. Dry mouth - The reduction in saliva production can lead to this uncomfortable condition. Constipation - Patients may experience reduced bowel motility as a side effect. Diarrhea - Conversely, some individuals may experience increased bowel movements. Proactive management of these symptoms is essential for maintaining comfort and adherence to treatment. It is imperative to discuss any persistent or severe gastrointestinal symptoms with a healthcare provider. Sleep Pattern Changes Ironically, some people find that their sleep gets a little disrupted in the beginning. You may have trouble falling asleep at first, wake up more than usual, or experience vivid dreams or nightmares. Some people wake up too early and cannot fall back asleep. Difficulty falling asleep - Onset of sleep could be delayed. Awakening during the night - There might be an increase in nighttime wakefulness. Unrefreshing sleep - Patients may not feel restored even after ample time spent asleep. Changes in REM sleep - There may be alterations in the timing and duration of REM cycles. Early morning awakening - Waking up prematurely and being unable to return to sleep is another possible effect. These changes may diminish over time with continued use of the medication. Acclimatization to Quviviq can vary, with some patients experiencing transient disruptions before stabilizing. Psychological Impact Quviviq may precipitate mood disturbances, heightening anxiety levels in susceptible individuals, thus warranting close monitoring. In some cases, dreams influenced by Quviviq can be vivid or distressing (dysphoric), contributing to disturbances in mental well-being, which could exacerbate preexisting anxiety or mood disorders. A minority of patients may experience "rebound insomnia" or "withdrawal effects" upon discontinuation of the medication. Mood and Mental Health Changes We asked Dr. Michael Grandner, Sleep Expert and Professor of Neuroscience and Physiological Sciences, about potential side effects of newer sleep medications. He says: Even newer medications require close monitoring. Side effects may vary widely depending on the person. In other words, while these medications can help with sleep, their effects are not one-size-fits-all and need to be closely monitored by a healthcare professional. Quviviq can cause changes in mood. Some people feel more anxious, irritable, or emotionally off. This is more likely if you already have a history of anxiety or depression. Unusual or emotionally intense dreams can also leave you feeling unsettled the next day. These effects are not common, but they are important to be aware of. If you notice any changes in how you feel emotionally, it is best to talk to your doctor. Potential for Dependence Quviviq is not considered addictive in the traditional sense, but your body can get used to it over time. If you take it regularly for a long period, your system may begin to rely on it to fall asleep. Stopping suddenly could lead to what’s known as rebound insomnia, where sleep becomes even more difficult, along with feelings of anxiety or low mood. These reactions are your body’s way of adjusting to the absence of the medication. It is important to understand that this kind of dependence is not the same as addiction. Addiction involves a psychological urge to keep using a substance despite harmful consequences. In the case of Quviviq, dependence refers to your body becoming used to its effects and struggling to function normally without it. Because of this, doctors usually recommend tapering off the medication gradually rather than quitting all at once. Planning ahead with your healthcare provider can help reduce any withdrawal effects and ensure you stop the medication safely, without disrupting your sleep long term. Dealing with Adverse Side Effects Quviviq also has some side effects. The moment you start experiencing it, the best thing to do is to let your doctor know immediately. The sooner you bring it up, the easier it is to make changes that help you feel better. Your doctor can adjust your dosage, suggest other options, or help you manage the symptoms more comfortably. It is also normal for some side effects to show up in the beginning as your body adjusts to the medicine. For many people, these fade over time. But if the symptoms stick around or start affecting your daily life, it might be worth revisiting your treatment plan and dosage. Sometimes the medication that works for one person does not work the same way for another, and that is okay. What matters most is finding a solution that feels right for you. Tips to Ease Side Effects Start low, go slow: Many doctors begin with a lower dose to see how your body responds before increasing it gradually Avoid mixing it with other medications: Taking other medications that also affect the brain can increase the risk of side effects Take it at the right time: Try to align your dose at the same time each day, with your regular bedtime so that it works when you actually want to sleep Add in CBT-I: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy for Insomnia is a proven, non-medication approach that can help improve sleep and reduce reliance on pills Check in regularly: Follow-up appointments help track your progress and allow your provider to tweak your plan if needed Add in sleep hygiene: Things like keeping a regular bedtime, avoiding screens at night, limiting caffeine and journaling can make a big difference in how well Quviviq works and how your body handles it Paying attention to how your body responds and staying in touch with your doctor can go a long way in making the experience smoother and safer. The goal is always to improve your sleep without creating new challenges along the way. When You Should Call Your Doctor Some side effects of the medication need immediate medical attention. If you notice any of the following, stop taking Quviviq and contact your healthcare provider as soon as possible: Signs of a serious allergic reaction, such as difficulty breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a severe rash Unusual behaviors during sleep, like sleepwalking, driving, eating, or other activities you do not remember in the morning Mood changes, especially if you start feeling depressed, experience anxiety that feels worse than usual, or have thoughts of self-harm Excessive daytime drowsiness that affects your ability to function or stay alert Mental fog or confusion that does not go away These symptoms are rare, but they are important to catch early. Your doctor can help adjust your treatment plan or recommend a safer alternative if needed. Your safety always comes first. Start Sleeping Better With Sleep Reset Today! If you’re looking for an entirely drug-free way to get better and deeper sleep, the Sleep Reset program can help. We use CBT-I principles to help you fall asleep and stay asleep all night. Our free sleep quiz can help you identify the underlying causes of your sleep problems, so you can find the best solution for you. Our program does not rely on harmful pills, melatonin or supplements, which means no grogginess, dependency, or long-term health risks. Instead of relying on quick fixes, we use proven techniques to address the root causes of your sleep issues and give you the long-term tools to manage your sleep. Our dedicated sleep coach will help you via daily text to provide accountability, support, and guidance. The Sleep Reset program is available on iOS and Android. Take the Sleep quiz now. Start with a home sleep test . Already diagnosed and want an easy, comfortable oral appliance? Schedule with us to get a prescription . title: Bank of Hawaii Affirms Its Dedication to Hawaii Island Communities with Two New Branches of Tomorrow
summary: Bank of Hawaii marked another milestone with the blessing of its two newest Branches of Tomorrow, one in Ka‘ū on Nov. 3 and the other in Kona on Nov. 10.
body_text: Bank of Hawaii marked another milestone with the blessing of its two newest Branches of Tomorrow, one in Ka‘ū on Nov. 3 and the other in Kona on Nov. 10. These branch renovations are part of the bank’s longstanding commitment to modernize branches in closely knit communities across the state of Hawaii and the West Pacific. Both Branches of Tomorrow have been well established in their communities for decades, with the Ka‘ū Branch first opening over a century ago in December 1922. The Kona Branch first opened in 1957 and moved to its current location in 2012. “Ka‘ū and Kona are home to our neighbors, our families, and the businesses that make Hawaii Island unique,” said Bank of Hawaii Chairman and CEO Peter Ho. “These Branches of Tomorrow reflect our commitment to provide welcoming spaces for meaningful conversations and trusted guidance. We’ve been here for generations, and we’re committed to serving the next ones with the same aloha.” The newly renovated 1,920 sq. ft. Ka‘ū Branch has been thoughtfully modernized to include two private Pili rooms for in-person or virtual consultations. The popular 24/7 ATM remains easily accessible on the exterior of the branch. A refreshed interior honors the community it serves with a shimmery black wall behind the tellers that represents the nearby black sand beach of Punalu‘u. The Ka‘ū Branch is open five days a week, Monday through Friday, from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The architect is Peter Vincent Architects. Upgrades to the 6,918 sq. ft. Kona Branch include six Pili rooms for consultations and Banklanai® with 24/7 ATM banking. A signature art piece placed at the entrance to the branch showcases the stunning waters and swirling currents of the Kona coastline. The upgraded branch is located in the Kona Commons Shopping Center and is open six days a week: Monday through Friday from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m., and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 1 p.m. The architect is MC3 Architects. It has long been Bank of Hawaii’s mission to provide for all communities, large and small, and support their evolving needs. With 51 branches system-wide, Bank of Hawaii is honored to be the only financial institution on all main Hawaiian islands and throughout the West Pacific. Bank of Hawaii is investing in the following Branch of Tomorrow transformations over a two-year period: • ‘Ele‘ele, Kauai (opened March 11, 2024) • Lahaina, Maui (May 12, 2025) • Tamuning, Guam (July 14, 2025) • Hāna, Maui (Aug. 11, 2025) • Ka‘ū, Hawaii Island (Nov. 3, 2025) • Kona, Hawaii Island (Nov 10, 2025) • Lāna‘i (2026) • Kaunakakai, Molokai (2026) Bank of Hawaii looks forward to sharing updates as these projects move forward via boh.com and its social media platforms Facebook, Instagram and X (formerly Twitter).

title: United Bank Welcomes Jimmy Kimbell as Greenville, South Carolina Market President
summary: GREENVILLE, S.C. – United Bank recently welcomed Jimmy Kimbell as the new Greenville market president. In this role, Kimbell will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production while ensuring the market's profitability and sustained growth. Additionally, Kimbell will play a pivotal leadership role in managing public relations efforts in Greenville, while also representing United Bank in the community through active participation in civic affairs and professional organizations.
body_text: Contact: Sameera Jordan Media Relations Manager Sameera.Jordan@BankWithUnited.com Facebook LinkedIn Email Twitter GREENVILLE, N.C. – United Bank recently welcomed Jimmy Kimbell as the new Greenville market president. In this role, Kimbell will lead strategic efforts to drive commercial and retail production while ensuring the market's profitability and sustained growth. Additionally, Kimbell will play a pivotal leadership role in managing public relations efforts in Greenville, while also representing United Bank in the community through active participation in civic affairs and professional organizations. “Upstate South Carolina has become one of the fastest growing industrial hubs in the Southeast, making it a very attractive growth market for United,” said United Bank Regional President Marshall Cooper. “Jimmy’s hiring signifies an exciting next step in the growth of the Bank’s broader Carolinas region, as we continue to invest in our people and business operations in the South. We believe Jimmy’s decades of experience, extensive history in the region, and expertise in relationship banking will be immensely valuable for United.” Kimbell will be based in United’s Poinsett office in Greer. Comprised of five United Bank branches, the Greenville Market covers Oconee, Pickens, Greenville, Spartanburg, Cherokee, Union, Laurens, Greenwood, Abbeville, and Anderson counties in South Carolina. Kimbell’s hiring reaffirms the Bank’s continued commitment to its Greenville Market. Kimbell has over 35 years of experience in the financial services industry with an extensive background leading commercial banking operations and driving growth. Prior to joining United, he held numerous executive leadership roles at community banking institutions across the state, including experience as president and chief executive officer, senior vice president, and regional executive. “United Bank excels at maintaining a relationship-focused banking model, while also increasing its size and scale to better serve customers with more sophisticated products and services,” said Kimbell. “Relationships are what have kept me in the banking industry for so long. Being presented with an opportunity like this – to continue serving my community and helping customers find the solutions to their unique financial needs, but now with the resources of a large bank – was a very attractive opportunity for me.” Kimbell received a Bachelor of Science in Financial Management from Clemson University, and he is a graduate of the American Bankers Association National Commercial Lending School and Stonier Graduate School of Banking. He has been actively involved in the community throughout his career and currently serves as board chairman of the Greeneville Housing Fund and is a board member of Touched by ALS. Kimbell, his wife Amy, and their two children – daughter Lawing and son Jackson, a rising sophomore at Clemson – reside in Greer. ABOUT UNITED BANK United Bank is a premier community bank and a subsidiary of United Bankshares, Inc. (NASDAQ: UBSI). United has consolidated assets of approximately $34 billion with over 240 offices located across North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Virginia, West Virginia, Maryland, Ohio, and Pennsylvania, as well as Washington D.C. The Bank is dedicated to growing the relationships it has built since 1839 and offering a competitive suite of banking and lending products, treasury management, wealth management, mortgage services, personal and business credit cards, and more. Learn more about United Bank.

title: 10 reasons agencies move beyond spreadsheets
summary: Spreadsheets work at first, then quietly start costing agencies time, money, and client trust. Here are the 10 clearest signs it's time for a real system.
body_text: It usually starts with one broken formula. Someone opens the master client tracker on a Monday morning and a column that's tracked revenue for two years is suddenly full of #REF! errors. Nobody knows who changed it. Nobody has time to fix it before the 10am client call. That moment repeats itself in agencies everywhere, just with different details. A missing tab. A client who saw a column they shouldn't have. A founder who's the only person who understands how the whole thing fits together. Spreadsheets aren't a bad tool. They're just the wrong tool once an agency crosses a certain size and complexity. Here are 10 reasons growing agencies move on from them, and what they move to instead. TL;DR Spreadsheets break down at a predictable point: multiple people editing, multiple clients needing visibility, and multiple projects running at once. The average company now runs 101 apps, according to Okta's 2025 Businesses at Work report, and spreadsheets are usually just one piece of that sprawl, not a fix for it. Knowledge workers lose close to an hour and a half a day switching between tools and deciding which one to use, per Asana's Work Innovation Lab research. Internal operations tools solve this by combining data, permissions, and client-facing views in one connected system. The fix isn't more spreadsheets or more point tools. It's one system built around how the agency actually delivers work. 1. Why do formulas keep breaking as the sheet grows? Every added column, hidden row, or copy-pasted formula is a small risk. One person fixes something for their own workflow and breaks a calculation three tabs away. Nobody notices until a report goes out with the wrong number on it. Spreadsheets were built for individual calculations, not shared operational systems with dozens of interdependent references. The bigger the sheet, the more fragile it gets. 2. Why does everything depend on one person to keep it running? Most agency spreadsheet systems have an architect: the founder or ops lead who built the formulas, knows which tab feeds which report, and quietly patches things when they break. If that person goes on leave, the system's institutional knowledge goes with them. This is founder dependency, and it's one of the clearest signs an agency has outgrown its tools rather than its team. 3. Why can't clients get real visibility without a separate report? Clients increasingly expect to see project status themselves, not wait for a weekly email update. Spreadsheets can't safely give that. Sharing a live sheet with a client risks exposing internal notes, other clients' data, or formulas they were never meant to see. So agencies build a second, simplified version just for clients, which means double the maintenance for the same information. 4. Why do multiple versions of the same file cause costly mistakes? "Client_Tracker_FINAL_v3_updated.xlsx" is a familiar joke because it's a familiar problem. Once a spreadsheet gets emailed, downloaded, or duplicated across a team, there's no single source of truth left. Someone works from a stale copy and makes a decision based on numbers that were already wrong. 5. Why does reporting take a full afternoon instead of a few clicks? Pulling together a monthly client or leadership report from scattered tabs means copying data, checking it hasn't shifted, reformatting it, and hoping nothing was missed. That's hours spent assembling information instead of acting on it. 6. Why do permissions get harder to manage as the team grows? Spreadsheet sharing is mostly all-or-nothing. Someone can see the tab or they can't, and controlling that at a granular, field-by-field level (this client sees their project status but not the margin column) isn't realistic at scale. As headcount grows, so does the risk of the wrong person seeing the wrong data. 7. Why do reminders and follow-ups still happen manually? Spreadsheets can't send a client a reminder when an approval is overdue or notify a project lead when a deadline is at risk. Someone has to notice, then chase it manually, which means things fall through the cracks exactly when the agency is busiest. 8. Why does the tool stack keep growing instead of shrinking? Spreadsheets rarely replace other tools. They usually sit alongside a project management app, a separate CRM, invoicing software, and a handful of point solutions bolted on to cover gaps. The average company now uses 101 apps, according to Okta's 2025 Businesses at Work report , and every added tool is another place data can drift out of sync with the spreadsheet that's supposed to be the source of truth. 9. Why does switching between tools eat into billable hours? Every jump between the spreadsheet, the project tool, the inbox, and the client portal costs focus, not just time. Asana's Work Innovation Lab found that workers lose 57 minutes a day just switching between tools , plus another 30 minutes deciding which tool to use for a given task. For a billable-hours business, that's real revenue leaking out through tab switching. 10. Why does the system stop matching how the agency actually delivers work? Spreadsheets are generic by design. They don't know what a client engagement, a project milestone, or a delivery workflow actually is; they just hold numbers and text. As an agency's delivery process matures, the gap between "what the spreadsheet can show" and "what the business actually needs to run on" keeps widening. How do internal operations tools fix this? An internal operations tool connects the pieces a spreadsheet can only approximate: client records, project data, permissions, and automations, all pulling from one database instead of scattered files. The team gets one place to work. Clients get a branded, permission-controlled view of only what's relevant to them. Nobody's afternoon disappears into manual reporting. For agencies already running on Airtable, this doesn't mean throwing that data away. Noloco can sit directly on top of an existing Airtable base, adding real interfaces, granular permissions, and client portals without a migration project. For agencies that have outgrown a patchwork of spreadsheets and disconnected tools entirely, it works as the consolidation step: one operating system instead of five separate logins. How does Noloco compare to other options agencies consider? Tool Built for agency delivery Client portal included Granular field-level permissions Pricing model Airtable ⚠️ Flexible database, not agency-specific by default ⚠️ Interfaces available, limited permission depth ❌ Basic sharing controls Per-seat monday.com ❌ Built for internal team work, not client delivery ❌ Client access usually an add-on ❌ Mostly role-based, not field-level Per-seat Retool ❌ Developer-first internal tool builder ❌ Requires custom build ⚠️ Possible, but needs engineering setup Per-user / usage-based Softr ⚠️ No-code builder, blank canvas by default ⚠️ Buildable, page-by-page permissions ❌ Managed page-by-page, not data-level Per-seat SmartSuite ⚠️ Generic work management, not agency-specific ❌ Not a core feature ⚠️ Role-based permissions Per-seat Noloco ✅ Pre-configured for client, project, and financial workflows ✅ Branded client portals included ✅ Field- and record-level permissions Flat active-user pricing ‍ Final thoughts Spreadsheets aren't the enemy. They're just not designed to be an operating system, and agencies that keep asking them to be one end up paying for it in founder time, client trust, and missed details. The agencies that move on aren't abandoning what they built; they're keeping the data and the process logic, and adding the structure, permissions, and client experience a spreadsheet was never built to provide. FAQ What's the first sign an agency has outgrown spreadsheets? Usually it's a near-miss: a formula breaks, a client sees data they shouldn't, or a report goes out with an error nobody caught in time. If that near-miss keeps happening, it's a systems problem, not a one-off mistake. Do agencies need to give up Airtable or Google Sheets to fix this? Not necessarily. Some agencies add a front-end layer on top of their existing Airtable base for client-facing views and permissions. Others consolidate into a single system once the spreadsheet stack becomes too fragmented to maintain. Both are valid paths depending on how far the agency has scaled. How long does it take to move off a spreadsheet-based system? It depends on complexity, but agency-ready platforms with pre-built templates typically get a firm to first value in days or weeks, not the months a from-scratch build usually takes. Is a project management tool enough to replace spreadsheets? Generic project management tools solve internal task tracking but usually don't handle client-facing portals, granular permissions, or financial data well without expensive add-ons. Agencies often end up needing a broader operations system rather than just a PM tool. What's the difference between an internal operations tool and a PSA platform? PSA (professional services automation) platforms are typically pre-built around project, resource, and financial tracking with less flexibility. Internal operations tools like Noloco let an agency configure the system around its own delivery process instead of adapting to a fixed structure. Does moving off spreadsheets require technical or engineering resources? No. Modern no-code operations platforms are built for teams without in-house developers, using visual builders instead of code. title: Dermal Matrices: What Features Matter Most For Time To Graft?
summary: Dermal matrices can support tissue generation and vascularization in full-thickness skin defects. But which features matter most when it comes to time to graft?
body_text: Barbara Nsiah Anderson, PhD Dermal matrices are commonly used to support tissue generation and vascularization in full-thickness skin defects. Numerous dermal matrices have been developed, ranging in composition from biological extracellular matrices to biosynthetic or synthetic polymers. Additionally, several dermal matrix manufacturing processes have been employed to tune microarchitectural features such as porosity and pore size. The composition and microarchitectural features impact the body’s ability to interact with the dermal matrix and timeline needed to develop a vascularized wound bed capable of supporting a skin graft for definitive closure. Dermal matrix microarchitecture and composition Each dermal matrix has a unique microarchitecture and composition. For example, Cohealyx ® is a bioengineered, uniformly porous dermal matrix composed of bovine dermis, which contains collagen I and III (Figure A).1 Cohealyx allows for timely introduction of Type I and III collagen, which are natural biological cues that provide critical signaling during the wound healing process.2 Collagen is biocompatible, bioactive, and well conserved across species, making it an ideal material for a dermal matrix.3 Because collagen structure and sequence are well conserved amongst species, a dermal matrix such as Cohealyx is not expected to illicit an inflammatory response post implantation.1,3 In fact, Cohealyx-treated wounds demonstrated a lower immune cell filtration compared to other commercially available dermal matrices in a pre-clinical study.1 Scanning electron microscopy analysis reveals the range of pore sizes in a synthetic dermal matrix composed of biodegradable polyurethane foam, which has a porosity of 90% (Figure B).1 In contrast, the electrospun resorbable fiber matrix, depicted in Figure C, composed of polyglactin 910 and polydioxanone5 is less porous compared to Cohealyx (Figure A) and the biodegradable polyurethane foam dermal matrix (Figure B). A xenogeneic dermal matrix composed of fish skin contains smaller pores and has a lower porosity than Cohealyx (Figure D).6,7,8 A central role in wound bed readiness Dermal matrices serve a central role in wound bed readiness. After implantation, dermal matrices fill the wound bed, provide structural support, scaffolding, and bioactive cues, including support of cellular infiltration and vascular tissue deposition important for the wound healing process. Immediately after implantation, host cells—including fibroblasts and endothelial cells—infiltrate the matrix, initiating collagen deposition and angiogenesis. Once the wound bed has developed sufficient vasculature, it is ready to graft. The time required to develop a vascular bed capable of supporting a skin graft is highly dependent on the composition and microarchitecture characteristics of the dermal matrix. A comparison of several biological and biosynthetic dermal matrices with varying microarchitectures demonstrated differential in-vitro endothelial cell proliferation and angiogenic factor expression at 36 hours and in-vivo pre-clinical vascularization outcomes at 10 days.9 Early clinical data supports the pre-clinical finding that Cohealyx can support graft readiness in less than 14 days post implantation.10 Alternatively, other biological, biosynthetic, and synthetic dermal matrices have demonstrated wound readiness ranging from weeks to months.11-13 In pre-clinical work utilizing a full-thickness porcine model, wounds treated with Cohealyx demonstrated increased presence of endothelial cell infiltration compared to wounds treated with a fish skin graft.1 This data correlated with visual matrix observation at day seven: All Cohealyx treated wounds had >75% integration, whereas only 20% of fish skin graft treated wounds had this level of integration. When these wounds were grafted, the Cohealyx-treated wounds had 98% percent of graft take, whereas the fish skin graft wounds that were not fully ready for grafting only had 68% graft take. Early clinical data supports the pre-clinical finding that Cohealyx can support graft readiness in less than 14 days post implantation.10 Alternatively, other biological, biosynthetic, and synthetic dermal matrices have demonstrated wound readiness ranging from weeks to months.11-13 As graft take and survival are driven by vascular support, the choice of dermal matrix plays a pivotal role in achieving good graft take outcomes and timely wound closure. Dermal matrices: Key takeaways Dermal matrix selection should consider microarchitecture, composition, integration time, and vascularization potential, as these directly affect time to graft. When early grafting is desired, matrices engineered for fast integration and rapid vascularization may offer a clinical advantage. Looking for more articles about dermal matrices? Read Strategic Wound Closure in Resource-Limited Trauma: A Pragmatic Approach or Accelerating Healing for Complex Wounds: How Cohealyx™ Advances Readiness to Autografting . About the author Barbara Nsiah Anderson, PhD, Director of Scientific Affairs at AVITA Medical, leads pre-clinical study design and evaluation of new products for expansion of AVITA Medical’s acute wound care portfolio. She managed and designed the pre-clinical studies which supported the 2024 FDA clearance of Cohealyx®. She was instrumental in the successful publication of Cohealyx pre-clinical data in the Cureus journal.5 Dr. Anderson holds a PhD in bioengineering, is a fellow of the American Institute for Medical and Biological Engineering (AIMBE) and an inventor on several patents.
